info.description:
This page provides documentation about the REST APIs provided by Orchestrator software. You can interact with Orchestrator software directly using this page.
For more information, usage guides, and open-source tools related to the HPE Aruba Networking EdgeConnect API, visit the HPE Aruba Networking Dev Hub.

Note : To execute an API, click on 'Try it out' button, provide the needed parameters and click the 'Execute' button.
Best Practice: Retrieve statistics from EdgeConnect appliances directly!
To ensure the best Orchestrator UI user experience for SD-WAN administrators, it is not recommended to retrieve statistics directly from the Orchestrator API. The API is not suited for high-frequency polling of granular statistics or “data replication” into an external data store for two reasons:
  1. The volume of data that is requested scales linearly with the number of EdgeConnect devices and the granularity of the requested statistics.
  2. Orchestrator does not have the resources for the load that frequent REST API calls would impose.
Orchestrator serves multiple purposes and has limited resources tuned to do many functions, including:
  • Supporting 5-50 concurrent users accessing the UI
  • Orchestrating policies across the SD-WAN fabric with 2 to 1,000 devices
  • Collecting and reporting statistics from these devices for Orchestrator users
For more information, please click here to review the "Integration Points for EdgeConnect Orchestrator and Gateways".

post.summary: Retrieve appliance alarms for specified appliances
post.description:
Returns active, historical, or all alarms for the appliances specified in the request body.

**Response:** Each alarm object includes severity, description, recommendedAction, source, type, timestamps, acknowledgement status, and more. See the ApplianceAlarmItem schema for full details.

**Filtering:** Use query parameters to filter by status (`view`), severity level, and time range (`from`/`to`). Results can be sorted by severity (`orderBySeverity`) and capped with `maxAlarms`.

**Severity values:** Response values are uppercase (`WARNING`, `MINOR`, `MAJOR`, `CRITICAL`), while the `severity` query parameter accepts lowercase (`warning`, `minor`, `major`, `critical`).

**Correlation fields:** The fields `sourceIp`, `destinationIp`, `peerId`, `hierarchy`, `isRoot`, `instanceId`, `sourceLabel`, `destinationLabel`, and `saCount` are always present in every alarm object, but only contain meaningful (non-default) values for correlation-engine alarm types: tunnel down, interface down, nexthop down, and IPSLA link down alarms. For all other alarm types, these fields contain default values (empty string for strings, `false` for booleans, `0` for numbers).

**Obtaining nePk values:** Appliance IDs (nePks) can be retrieved from `GET /appliance`. Each appliance object contains an `id` field in the format `{number}.NE` (e.g., `10.NE`, `2094.NE`).

**Note on hostName:** The `hostName` field is populated from the appliance's configured hostname. In rare cases during alarm creation, if the appliance is not in cache, it may be empty. Resolve via `GET /appliance` if needed.

put.description:
Updates an existing cipher profile with new cryptographic settings. The profile must be editable (built-in profiles like Default, FIPS, CSfC cannot be modified). If the profile is active, changes are immediately written to configuration files. Requires READ_WRITE role.

**Validation Rules:**
- Profile name: required, max 32 characters, must be unique
- Comments: optional, max 512 characters
- TLS cipher suites and named curves: required, use 'ALL' or specific values from /defaultCipherParameters
- TLS minDHParamKeySize: -1 (default) or 2048-4096 in 1024 increments
- Tunnel IKE minPskLength: 8-64 characters
- Certificate minRSAKeySize: -1, 2048, 3072, or 4096
- Certificate minEcKeyLen: -1, 256, 384, or 521
- All algorithm arrays must have at least one value
- PQC (Post-Quantum Cryptography): TLS named curves with PQC hybrid key exchange require a TLS 1.3 cipher suite to also be enabled
-  tunnel.ike.pqcKeyExchangeMandatory requires at least one PQC group in tunnel.ike.dhGroup
-  certificate.supportedPQCAlgorithms values must be present in CERT_PQC_ALGORITHMS and require a TLS 1.3 cipher suite

Retrieves the full deployment configuration for a specified EdgeConnect appliance. This is the first step of the read-modify-write workflow for changing any deployment setting (interfaces, DHCP, routing, etc.). When cached is true, returns data from Orchestrator's database (faster, may be stale). When cached is false, fetches live data directly from the appliance (slower, always current). Use cached=false when retrieving a config you intend to modify. To apply changes after modifying the returned object, POST the full modified deployment JSON to `POST /appliance/rest?nePk={nePk}&url=deployment` (see the 'appliance' tag). **Key data paths:** Interface configs are in `modeIfs[].applianceIPs[]`. DHCP server config (including DNS servers) is at `modeIfs[].applianceIPs[].dhcpd.server.dns`. Interface label/zone/vrf fields are numeric IDs — resolve to names via `sysConfig.ifLabels`, `sysConfig.zones`, and `sysConfig.vrfs`. Requires 'read' or 'read-write' role.

Returns full configuration with customDefaultIP, internalManagementIP, and label mappings. The defaultIPOrDns field is excluded (set to null) in this endpoint.

**With nePk parameter:**
Returns resolved IP/domain for the specified appliance using this priority:

2. Otherwise returns customDefaultIP if set, or first internalManagementIP

**Container Mode:**
When Orchestrator runs in container mode, internalManagementIP is empty since the container's internal IP cannot be used for appliance connectivity.

post.description:
Updates the Orchestrator IP/domain that appliances use to connect.

**Behavior:**
- If `customDefaultIP` is empty, appliances use Orchestrator's internal management IP
- Label entries allow different IPs for appliances based on WAN interface labels
- Lower priority numbers are checked first (priority 1 before priority 2)
- The `internalManagementIP` field is ignored in requests (auto-populated by Orchestrator)

**Validation Rules:**
- `customDefaultIP` and label `ipOrDns` must not contain slashes (not full URLs)
- Priority values must be non-negative integers (>= 0)
- Label field must be a non-null object (use empty object {} if no labels needed)
- In container mode, `customDefaultIP` cannot be empty

**Side Effects:**
- Action is logged to system action log with user and data details
- Changes affect appliance connectivity on next configuration sync

post.summary: Save or update HA groups configuration
post.description: Creates or updates the complete High Availability (HA) groups configuration. This is a replace operation - the entire HA groups configuration will be overwritten with the provided data. Each HA group pairs two appliances for redundancy and failover. Validation rules: (1) Each group requires exactly 2 appliances, (2) Each appliance must have valid haSyncInfo, (3) An appliance cannot appear in multiple groups, (4) The subnet/mask must provide at least 32 subnets for HA interfaces. Both appliances must be in inline-router mode. Actions are logged to the system audit trail.

post.summary: Save or replace the Mist registration code
post.description: Stores the Mist WAN Assurance registration code on Orchestrator, replacing any existing value. The code must be a JWT consisting of three dot-separated Base64url segments. The payload (middle segment) must be valid JSON containing the required claims: `org_id`, `svc`, `provider`, `env`, `epterm_url`, `iat`, `exp`. The `exp` claim must be a future Unix timestamp (in seconds). Requires READ_WRITE role permission. Changes are written to the audit trail.

Common reasons: missing or empty `registrationCode`, malformed JWT (not three dot-separated Base64url segments), payload is not valid JSON, one or more required claims (`org_id`, `svc`, `provider`, `env`, `epterm_url`, `iat`, `exp`) are missing, or `exp` is in the past.

401.description: Unauthorized — authentication required or invalid credentials.

403.description: Forbidden — user lacks READ_WRITE role permission.

post.summary: Retrieve real-time tunnel stats, flow stats, packet drop stats (with reason codes), DSCP stats, traffic class stats, shaper stats, and interface stats from an EdgeConnect appliance for monitoring scripts and alerting
post.description:
Real-time monitoring API for tunnel bandwidth, TCP/UDP flow counts, packet drops, QoS shaper metrics, DSCP traffic, traffic class throughput, and interface bandwidth. Poll faster than every 3 seconds to avoid data gaps.

**Common Use Cases:**
- Build monitoring scripts that poll this API at configurable polling intervals
- Set up threshold-based alerting when packet drops exceed a defined threshold
- Track packet drop reason codes to identify specific network issues
- Monitor consecutive polling intervals to trigger alerts on persistent problems
- Create real-time dashboards with input parameters for EdgeConnect appliance metrics

**Statistics Types:**

| Type | name | filter | Description |
|------|------|--------|-------------|
| tunnel | tunnel name, 'pass-through', or 'pass-through-unshaped' | not used | Returns per-tunnel tx/rx bytes, packets, and MOS scores for voice quality monitoring on overlay tunnels. |
| trafficType | '0' (optimized) or '3' (all-traffic) | not used | Returns aggregate bandwidth metrics across all optimized WAN-accelerated traffic or all traffic types combined. |
| dscp | '0' to '63' | required | Returns per-DSCP marking statistics to monitor QoS policy effectiveness and traffic classification by differentiated services code point. |
| trafficClass | '0' to '9' | required | Returns per-traffic-class throughput and packet counts to verify business intent traffic prioritization (class 0 is highest priority). |
| flow | '0' (TCP accel), '1' (TCP unaccel), '2' (non-TCP) | required (use '3' for all traffic) | Returns flow metrics: CREATED (flows created/sec), DELETED (flows deleted/sec), EXISTING (active flows), MAX (peak flows), plus byte/packet counters. |
| shaper | '0' to '9' (traffic class) | 0=outbound, 1=inbound | Returns QoS shaper queue depth, throughput, and shaped traffic metrics per traffic class for outbound or inbound direction. |
| drops | '' (empty string) | not used | Returns packet drop counters with reason codes to identify congestion, policy drops, or interface errors across the appliance. |
| interface | interface name (e.g., 'wan0') | required | Returns per-interface tx/rx bytes, packets, and error counters for physical and logical interfaces like wan0, lan0, or bvi0. |

**Internal Drop Reason Codes (for type=drops):**

The response keys are numeric reason codes (1-399). The complete code-to-description mapping is available in the `x-drop-reason-codes` extension on the RealTimeStatsResponse schema. Common categories include:

| Code Range | Category |
|------------|----------|
| 1-27 | LAN Rx/Tx errors (pass-through, packet length, tunnel, policy, checksum, queue full, buffer) |
| 28-57 | WAN Rx/Tx errors (tunnel, TPH, frame, queue full, checksum, flow state, SYN, buffer) |
| 58-77 | NAT, MTU, FEC, fragmentation errors |
| 78-88 | QoS drops (packet expired, tunnel down, bad flow, enqueue full - egress/ingress) |
| 89-101 | Packet/stream encode/decode/transform errors |
| 102-113 | FRED/FMST flow errors |
| 114-135 | IPsec and TCP errors |
| 136-140 | ZCI and kernel errors |
| 141-165 | License, control packets, NAT, overlay errors |
| 166-177 | Routing errors (no route, TTL, bridge, VXLAN, FEC framing) |
| 178-189 | QoS flow errors, security policy drops |
| 190-213 | ICMP, tunnel, bridge port, VRF errors |
| 214-260 | Local packet errors, hash collisions, multicast, WTX encap |
| 261-293 | Zone/VRF, IDS/IPS, segmentation, IPSec queue errors |
| 294-339 | ZCI internal errors, datapath overflow, FPOC fragment errors |
| 340-399 | FPOC cleanup, DDOS, VXLAN, tracert, OTO, IDS inline, bridge/switch errors |

To get the live code mapping from a specific appliance, call `stats/drops/meta/info` via the appliance proxy API.

**Filter Values (string):** '0'=optimized_traffic, '1'=pass_through_shaped, '2'=pass_through_unshaped, '3'=all_traffic

**Response Format:** `{'metric': [[timestamp, value], ...]}` with up to 3 data points.

**Authorization:** READ or READ_WRITE role.

post.summary: Create or update a template group
post.description:
Creates a new template group from an existing one or updates an existing template group's configuration. When the request body 'name' matches the 'templateGroup' query parameter, the endpoint updates the existing group. When they differ, a new template group is created using templates from the source group. QoS templates require a valid license.

**Deployment behavior:** There is no separate deploy/apply endpoint. Modifying a template group here or changing selections via `POST /template/templateSelection` automatically queues all associated appliances for orchestration. To determine which appliances are affected, call `GET /template/applianceAssociation` (no nePk) and find appliances whose templateIds include the modified group name.

**Monitoring orchestration completion:** After a POST, poll `GET /template/history?nePk=<id>&latestOnly=true` for each affected appliance. When the response includes a history entry for the modified template name with `appliedOn` timestamp newer than your POST time and `status` of 'successful', orchestration is complete for that appliance. If no new entry appears within your timeout, the appliance may still be pending or unreachable.

**User Management template:** The 'users' template contains a map of local appliance user accounts keyed by username. Each user has fields: `self`, `enable`, `gid`, `password`, `gms_marked`. Passwords are redacted (empty string) on GET; supply the new password in `valObject` on POST. Use `GET /userAccount?nePk=<id>` to verify user changes were applied to an appliance.

**Related endpoints:** Associate groups with appliances via `POST /template/applianceAssociation`. Check which groups an appliance has via `GET /template/applianceAssociation?nePk=<id>`.

parameters.name: templateGroup
parameters.description: Target template group name. Must not be empty. If this matches the 'name' in the request body, the group is updated; otherwise a new group is created.

createNew.summary: Create a new template group from source

requestBody.description: Template group configuration containing the source group name (for cloning) or target group name (for updating) and the templates to save.

cloneGroup.description: When name differs from templateGroup query param, creates a new group

updateUserManagement.description: Updates the 'users' (User Management) template to change or add a local user account password. The valObject.users map is keyed by username. Passwords are redacted (empty string) on GET but must be supplied on POST. This automatically queues associated appliances for orchestration — no separate deploy call is needed. Verify via GET /template/history?nePk=<id>&latestOnly=true or GET /userAccount?nePk=<id>.

get.summary: Gets all Zscaler Tunnels with IP SLA's status of the appliance. The response contains <nePk_labelId>, <connectionStatus> map.
get.description:
Retrieves the real-time connection status of all Zscaler third-party tunnels configured on the specified appliance. The status is determined using IP SLA (Service Level Agreement) monitoring which tracks the health of each tunnel.

**Connection Status Values:**
- **Up**: Both primary and secondary tunnels (if configured) are operational
- **Down**: All configured tunnels are not operational
- **1 of 2 Up**: Only one of the two configured tunnels is operational (partial connectivity)
- **Deleting**: The tunnel configuration is being removed
- **Appliance Unreachable**: Unable to communicate with the appliance to determine tunnel status

**Response Structure:**
The response is a key-value map where:
- **Key**: Composite identifier in format `<nePk>_<labelId>` representing the appliance and interface
- **Value**: One of the connection status values listed above

**Use Cases:**
- Monitor Zscaler tunnel health for specific appliances
- Detect partial connectivity issues (1 of 2 tunnels up)
- Identify unreachable appliances in the network
- Track tunnel deletion progress

get.summary: Get sparse tunnel link status pairs for an overlay network (v2)
get.description: Returns tunnel link status as sparse array-of-pairs grouped by status, replacing the dense N×N matrix from v1. The response contains linkInfo[status] = [[srcIndex, destIndex], ...] where each [srcIndex, destIndex] pair references indices into the nePks array. Status codes: 0=NO_TUNNEL, 1=UP, 2=PARTIALLY_DOWN, 3=DOWN, 4=NO_STATUS. Payload size is O(T) where T is the number of tunnel connections, compared to O(N²) in v1. No appliance count threshold — works at any scale. Supports ETag-based caching.

HaAppliance.description: Appliance configuration within an HA group.

haIf.description: HA interface name used for cross-connection between HA pair appliances.

appliances.description: Array of exactly 2 appliances forming the HA pair. Both appliances must be in inline-router mode.

subnet.description: IPv4 subnet for allocating IPs to internal HA VLAN interfaces. Must provide minimum 32 subnets based on mask.

mask.description: Subnet mask for carving IP blocks from the HA subnet. Used to create smaller subnets for each HA interface.

vlanStart.description: Starting VLAN ID for internal HA VLAN interfaces. Increments by 1 for each additional VLAN interface.

v6HaSubnet.description: IPv6 subnet for HA interfaces. Used when appliances have IPv6 WAN interfaces (requires appliance version 9.6.0+).

v6HaMask.description: IPv6 subnet mask for HA interfaces. Used when v6HaSubnet is configured.

HaGroups.description: Map of HA group IDs to their configurations. Keys are string representations of group IDs.

HaSyncInfo.description: HA synchronization configuration for persistent connection between paired appliances.

haSyncInterface.description: HA sync interface name with VLAN tag (e.g., 'wan1.999').

localIP.description: Local IP address for HA sync connection. Must be in the configured HA subnet.

peerIP.description: Peer appliance IP address for HA sync connection. Must be in the configured HA subnet.

vlanMask.description: VLAN subnet mask for the HA sync interface. Typically matches the group mask value.

nePk.description: Network Element Primary Key - unique appliance identifier assigned by Orchestrator. Format: '<id>.NE'.

endEntityProfileConfigStructure.description: End Entity Profile configuration for certificate enrollment and management.

label.description: Unique identifier for the End Entity Profile. Must be unique across all profiles (case-insensitive comparison).

purpose.description: Defines the certificate usage type. Determines how the certificate will be used by appliances.

csr_attrs.description: Certificate Signing Request attributes specifying the cryptographic algorithm. Must be compatible with the active Cipher Profile's minimum key lengths (RSA/ECDSA) or supported PQC algorithms (ML-DSA).

est.description: Indicates if EST (Enrollment over Secure Transport) is enabled. Automatically set to true when est_server_profiles contains entries.

est_server_profiles.description: Mapping of EST Server profiles by priority (0-3). Priority 0 is highest. Must have at least one entry if EST is enabled.

0.description: Primary EST Server profile name (highest priority). Must reference an existing EST Profile in Orchestrator.

1.description: Secondary EST Server profile name (second priority). Used as fallback if primary fails.

2.description: Tertiary EST Server profile name (third priority). Used if both primary and secondary fail.

3.description: Quaternary EST Server profile name (lowest priority). Last resort fallback option.

global_subject_host_domain.description: Domain suffix appended to hostname in certificate subject. Example: hostname 'xyz-ecva' with domain 'test.com' produces 'xyz-ecva.test.com' in subject.

global_san_host_domain.description: Domain suffix appended to hostname in certificate SAN (Subject Alternative Name) DNS field.

global_san_ip_interface.description: Interface label whose IP address will be added to certificate SAN. Must match a configured interface label (e.g., MPLS1, INET1).

global_san_email_domain.description: Domain suffix appended to hostname for email (RFC822) field in certificate SAN. Example: hostname 'xyz-ecva' with domain 'test.com' produces 'xyz-ecva@test.com'.

organization.description: Organization name (O) field for the certificate subject DN.

organizational_unit_name.description: Organizational Unit name (OU) field for the certificate subject DN.

subject_use_serial.description: When true, includes the appliance serial number in the certificate subject DN.

HAInfoObj.description: Orchestrator High Availability information object containing mode and instance details.

primaryInstance.description: Primary orchestrator instance details. Null when mode is NORMAL. Contains the active orchestrator handling all orchestration tasks.

currentInstance.description: Current orchestrator instance details. Null when mode is NORMAL. Represents the instance responding to this request.

HANotificationConfigObj.description: Configuration for HA cluster email notifications when instance health checks fail.

enabledEmailNotification.description: Whether email alerts are enabled for HA instance failures. When enabled, emailAddress must be provided.

InstanceIpOrDNS.description: Mapping of an orchestrator instance to its reachability address (IP or DNS name).

instanceId.description: Unique identifier of the orchestrator instance. Must match an existing registered HA instance ID.

labelId.description: Unique identifier of the label for which this reachability config applies. Must reference an existing label ID.

priority.description: Priority order for applying label configs. Lower values have higher priority. Must be unique across all label configs.

instances.description: IP/DNS addresses for reaching each orchestrator instance. Must include all registered HA instances.

OrchHAInstance.description: Orchestrator HA instance representing a single orchestrator in the HA cluster.

id.description: Unique identifier for this orchestrator instance. Used for tracking and management.

name.description: Human-readable name of the orchestrator instance. Configured during HA setup.

PrimaryStatus.description: Primary orchestrator HTTP reachability status response object.

tool_result.description: Results from tool execution to continue AI workflow. Requires msg_id when present.

x-deployment-behavior.onPremises: Returns true - admin user exists in user management table
x-deployment-behavior.container: Returns false - no built-in admin user in cloud deployments

PlatformInfo.description: Response object containing the deployment platform type of the Orchestrator server.

x-enum-descriptions.UNKNOWN: On-premises or undetected platform (default when platform.conf is missing)

StatisticsP99.description: Performance statistics object containing P99 percentile timing metrics. Computed from the last 300 runs of a task with 1 decimal precision.

max.description: Maximum execution time in milliseconds across sampled runs.

p99.description: 99th percentile execution time in milliseconds. 99% of runs completed within this time.

maxReadable.description: Human-readable maximum time in seconds format.

avgReadable.description: Human-readable average time in seconds format.

p99Readable.description: Human-readable P99 time in seconds format.

count.description: Number of task executions included in the statistics sample (max 300).

StatsRetentionInfo.description: Represents retention configuration for a specific statistics type and time granularity. Used to manage how long flow statistics data is retained in the database.

statType.description: The type of statistics (e.g., 'flow', 'tunnel', 'interface'). Identifies the category of data this retention setting applies to.

defaultRetention.description: Default retention period in seconds. For hourly flow stats, fixed at 7776000 seconds (90 days).

parentGroup.description: Optional sorted array of parent group names for hierarchical grouping.

ApplicationGroupSearchResponse.description: Set of application group names matching the search pattern, sorted alphabetically

items.description: Application group name

ApplicationGroupsRequest.description: Request body for creating/updating application groups. Keys are group names (alphanumeric, hyphen, underscore; max 31 chars).

ApplicationGroupsResponse.description: A map of application group names to their configuration. Each key is a user-defined group name.

ApplicationNamesResponse.description: Sorted array of unique application names matching the search pattern.

items.description: Application name.

ApplicationWildcardEntry.description: Request object for wildcard application search.

pattern.description: Wildcard pattern to match application names. Supports standard wildcard characters. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed automatically.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 30 if not specified or set to 0.

CloudAppSubnet.description: IP subnet information for a cloud application, including reachability probe configuration.

subnet.description: Cloud application IP subnet in CIDR notation (e.g., 173.240.103.64/26).

reachableIp.description: First known reachable IP address from the subnet for connectivity probing.

pingMethod.description: Protocol used to probe reachability of the subnet. Valid values: TCP, UDP.

pingPort.description: Port number used for reachability probing (e.g., 80, 443).

ConfidenceEntriesResponse.description: Map of application names to their confidence entries.

DeleteSuccessResponse.description: Success response for delete operations on confidence entries.

message.description: Confirmation message indicating the confidence entry was successfully deleted.
message.example: Successfully deleted user defined confidence entry for salesforce

DomainNameUserEntry.description: Configuration object for a user-defined DNS-based application classification entry

domain.description: The domain name pattern for traffic classification. Used to match DNS requests for application identification.

name.description: Application name for this domain classification. Must be alphanumeric with hyphens, underscores, or dots allowed.

description.description: Optional description for the application. Cannot contain the pipe character '|'.

priority.description: Classification priority for conflict resolution. Higher values indicate higher priority when multiple rules match.

disabled.description: Whether this classification rule is disabled. Disabled rules are not applied to traffic.

ModeUpdateResponse.description: Response returned when application group mode is successfully changed.

message.description: Success message confirming mode change.
message.example: Application mode update successfully

data.description: Optional migration data returned when switching modes. Contains information about groups that could not be automatically migrated.

NotFoundResponse.description: Response when appliance or feature is not found.

error.description: Error message for not found scenarios.

ERROR.description: Error code when feature is not available.

PostSuccessResponse.description: Response returned when DNS classification is successfully created or updated.

message.description: Success message confirming the creation or update of the DNS classification record.

SuccessResponse.description: Successful response containing async operation handle

value.description: Client key (poll handle) for tracking the asynchronous operation status. Use this key to poll for operation completion.

appTagsBody.description: Legacy schema - use ApplicationGroupsRequest instead. Request body for creating or updating application groups.

autoUpdates.description: Auto-update toggle settings for each application classification pipeline. Each field controls whether that classification type is automatically updated from the Cloud Portal.

portProtocolClassification.description: Auto-update toggle for IP/TCP/UDP port-protocol classification definitions.

dnsClassification.description: Auto-update toggle for DNS/domain-name classification definitions.

ipIntelligenceClassification.description: Auto-update toggle for IP intelligence (address map) classification definitions.

meterFlowClassification.description: Auto-update toggle for meter flow classification definitions.

compoundClassification.description: Auto-update toggle for compound classification definitions.

saasClassification.description: Auto-update toggle for SaaS application classification definitions.

compound.description: Compound application definition for multi-attribute traffic classification. Combines multiple matching criteria to identify network applications.

id.description: Unique identifier for the compound rule. IDs > 50000 are user-modified portal records. Must match query parameter.

name.description: Application name. Required, alphanumeric/hyphen/underscore only, max 31 characters.

confidence.description: Classification confidence level. Higher values increase match priority.

description.description: Optional description of the rule. Cannot contain pipe character '|'.
description.example: Custom application for internal HTTPS traffic

disabled.description: When true, the rule is inactive and will not be used for classification.

protocol.description: Transport protocol filter. Common values: 'tcp', 'udp'. Empty string to skip.

dst_port.description: Destination port filter. Accepts single port, range, or comma-separated list. Examples: '443', '80-443', '22,80,443'. Empty to skip.

src_port.description: Source port filter. Accepts single port, range, or comma-separated list. Mutually exclusive with either_port. Empty to skip.

either_port.description: Matches traffic with port in either direction. Mutually exclusive with src_port/dst_port. Empty to skip.

dst_ip.description: Destination IPv4 filter. Accepts CIDR notation or range. Examples: '10.0.0.0/8', '192.168.1.1-254'. Comma-separated for multiple. Empty to skip.

src_ip.description: Source IPv4 filter. Accepts CIDR notation or range. Mutually exclusive with either_ip. Empty to skip.

either_ip.description: Matches traffic with IP in either direction. Mutually exclusive with src_ip/dst_ip. Empty to skip.

dst_dns.description: Destination DNS/domain filter. Supports wildcards (e.g., '*.example.com'). Mutually exclusive with either_dns. Empty to skip.

src_dns.description: Source DNS/domain filter. Supports wildcards. Mutually exclusive with either_dns. Empty to skip.

either_dns.description: Matches traffic with DNS in either direction. Mutually exclusive with src_dns/dst_dns. Empty to skip.

dst_service.description: Destination SaaS service filter. Use service name or organization identifier. Empty to skip.

src_service.description: Source SaaS service filter. Mutually exclusive with either_service. Empty to skip.

either_service.description: Matches traffic with service in either direction. Mutually exclusive with src_service/dst_service. Empty to skip.

dst_geo.description: Destination geographic location filter. Use country/region codes (e.g., 'US', 'EU'). Empty to skip.

src_geo.description: Source geographic location filter. Mutually exclusive with either_geo. Empty to skip.

either_geo.description: Matches traffic with geo location in either direction. Mutually exclusive with src_geo/dst_geo. Empty to skip.

vlan.description: VLAN/interface filter for matching traffic on specific network segments. Empty to skip.

dscp.description: DSCP (Differentiated Services Code Point) filter. Values 0-63 for QoS marking match. Empty to skip.

dnsConfig.description: Request body for creating or updating a DNS-based application classification.

domain.description: The DNS domain name or hostname to classify. Must match the domain query parameter.

name.description: Application name for this domain. Alphanumeric, hyphen, underscore, and period characters only. Maximum 31 characters.

description.description: Optional description for the application. Cannot contain the pipe character '|'.

priority.description: Classification priority. Higher values take precedence when multiple rules match.

disabled.description: When true, this classification rule is disabled and will not be applied.

dnsConfig2.description: Request object for deleting a DNS-based application definition.

domain.description: The domain name to delete from application definitions. Must be a valid domain without leading slashes. Example: 'example.com' or 'subdomain.example.com'.

ipIntelligence.description: IP Intelligence Classification entry representing an application definition for an IP address range.

ip_start.description: Starting IPv4 address in 32-bit unsigned integer format. Must match the ipStart query parameter. Valid range: 0 to 4294967295.

ip_end.description: Ending IPv4 address in 32-bit unsigned integer format. Must be >= ip_start and match the ipEnd query parameter. Valid range: 0 to 4294967295.

name.description: Application name. Required field that must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, underscores, or periods. Maximum length: 31 characters.

description.description: Optional description of the application. Cannot contain pipe (|), newline, or carriage return characters.

country.description: Country name associated with the IP range. Cannot contain pipe (|), newline, or carriage return characters.

country_code.description: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Cannot contain pipe (|), newline, or carriage return characters.

org.description: Organization name associated with the IP range. Cannot contain pipe (|), newline, or carriage return characters.

priority.description: Classification priority/confidence level. Higher values indicate higher confidence. Valid range: 1 to 100.

subattributes.description: JSON-formatted string containing additional application attributes. If empty or '{}', default values are applied. Must include required keys: msinstance, mscategory, proxy.

ipIntelligenceConfidence.description: IP Intelligence confidence entry for overriding portal-provided Address Map priority.

name.description: Application name identifier. Must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, underscores, or periods.

priority.description: Confidence priority value for the application. Higher values indicate greater confidence in application classification.

meterFlow.description: DPI meter flow application definition object for configuring application classification settings.

flowType.description: Meter flow type identifier. Must be 'MF' for meter flow applications. Must match the flowType query parameter.

mid.description: Unique meter flow identifier. Must correspond to an existing DPI application ID from portal template data and match the mid query parameter.

name.description: Application name. Must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, underscores, or periods. Maximum length is 31 characters. Cannot be modified for existing entries.

description.description: Optional description for the meter flow application. Cannot contain the pipe character '|'.
description.example: Custom meter flow application for traffic classification

priority.description: Classification priority value. Higher values indicate higher priority. Range: 1-100.

disabled.description: Whether the meter flow application is disabled. Set to true to disable classification for this application.

portProtocol.description: Port protocol classification entry for user-defined application

port.description: Port number for the application. Use '0' for IP Protocol applications. Must match the port query parameter.

protocol.description: Protocol number. Use 6 for TCP, 17 for UDP. For IP Protocol apps (port=0), use the IP protocol number (e.g., 47 for GRE).

name.description: Application name. Must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, underscores, or periods. Maximum 31 characters.

description.description: Optional description for the application. Cannot contain the pipe character '|'.

priority.description: Classification priority. Higher values indicate higher priority when multiple rules match.

disabled.description: Whether the classification rule is disabled. Set to true to disable without deleting.

saasId.description: Unique identifier for the SaaS application. Use -1 to create a new application. User-defined applications must have ID >= 25000.

application.description: Name of the SaaS cloud application. Must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, or underscores. Maximum 31 characters.

domains.description: Array of domain names associated with this SaaS application. Required and cannot be empty. Supports wildcards (e.g., *.example.com).

addresses.description: Array of subnet entries defining IP ranges for this SaaS application. Required and cannot be empty.

threshold.description: RTT (Round Trip Time) threshold value in milliseconds for SaaS performance monitoring.

ports.description: Array of port numbers as strings associated with this SaaS application.

enabled.description: Internal flag indicating if the SaaS application is enabled. Typically set to false for user-defined applications.

processedAt.description: Internal timestamp indicating when the entry was last processed. Set automatically by the system.

Auth.description: Complete authentication configuration containing AAA settings, RADIUS, and TACACS+ server configurations.

radius.description: RADIUS server configuration for remote authentication.

tacacs.description: TACACS+ server configuration for remote authentication.

name.description: Authentication method name. Valid values: 'local', 'radius', 'tacacs'.

self.description: Priority order of this authentication method (1-3). Lower number = higher priority.

AuthConfigMap.description: Map of authentication methods keyed by priority order (1-3). Maximum 3 methods allowed.

AuthorConfigElement.description: Authorization configuration settings for user mapping and defaults.

default-user.description: Default user role assigned when remote authorization fails. Common values: 'monitor', 'admin'.

map-order.description: Order for resolving user permissions. Values: 'remote-first' (check remote then local), 'local-only' (only local).

RADIUSConfig.description: RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) configuration container.

server.description: Map of RADIUS server configurations keyed by priority order.

address.description: IP address or hostname of the RADIUS server.

auth-port.description: UDP port for RADIUS authentication. Standard port is 1812.

enable.description: Whether this RADIUS server is enabled for authentication.

key.description: Shared secret key for RADIUS server communication. Displayed as masked value in responses.

retransmit.description: Number of retry attempts before failing over to next server. Range: 1-10.

self.description: Priority order of this RADIUS server (1-3). Lower number = higher priority.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds waiting for RADIUS server response. Range: 1-60.

RADIUSConfigMap.description: Map of RADIUS servers keyed by priority order (1-3). Maximum 3 servers allowed.

TACACSConfig.description: TACACS+ (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus) configuration container.

server.description: Map of TACACS+ server configurations keyed by priority order.

address.description: IP address or hostname of the TACACS+ server.

auth-port.description: TCP port for TACACS+ authentication. Standard port is 49.

auth-type.description: Authentication protocol type. Values: 'pap' (Password Authentication Protocol), 'chap' (Challenge Handshake), 'ascii'.

enable.description: Whether this TACACS+ server is enabled for authentication.

key.description: Shared secret key for TACACS+ server communication. Displayed as masked value in responses.

retransmit.description: Number of retry attempts before failing over to next server. Range: 1-10.

self.description: Priority order of this TACACS+ server (1-3). Lower number = higher priority.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds waiting for TACACS+ server response. Range: 1-60.

TACACSConfigMap.description: Map of TACACS+ servers keyed by priority order (1-3). Maximum 3 servers allowed.

aaaConfig.description: AAA configuration containing authentication method order and authorization settings.

auth_method.description: Map of authentication methods in priority order (1-3).

author.description: Authorization configuration including default user and mapping order.

AutoTunedPropertiesResponse.description: Auto-tuned performance configuration properties for the orchestrator. All values are integers representing current recommended settings based on the managed appliance count.

threadPoolSize.description: Maximum size of the orchestrator's main thread pool for executing background tasks. Scales from 800 (≤1000 appliances) to 2800 (7000+ appliances).

ParallelOrchestrationTasks.description: Maximum concurrent orchestration tasks (e.g., configuration deployments, template applications). Scales from 50 (≤200 appliances) to 550 (7000+ appliances).

ParallelActionTasks.description: Maximum concurrent action tasks (e.g., appliance commands, operations). Scales from 100 (≤200 appliances) to 1100 (7000+ appliances).

ParallelReachabilityTasks.description: Maximum concurrent reachability check tasks for monitoring appliance connectivity. Scales from 20 (≤200 appliances) to 275 (7000+ appliances).

jettyMaxThreads.description: Maximum number of Jetty web server threads for handling HTTP requests. Scales from 600 (≤200 appliances) to 21000 (7000+ appliances).

availabilityThresholdSettings.description: Configuration for availability threshold settings across five network health categories. Each category defines limits that classify metrics as Good, Ok, or Poor.

overlayAvailability.description: Thresholds for SD-WAN overlay tunnel uptime percentage.

underlayAvailability.description: Thresholds for physical/logical WAN link uptime percentage.

networkRoleAvailability.description: Thresholds for network role (hub, spoke, mesh-node) uptime percentage.

interfaceAvailability.description: Thresholds for LAN/WAN interface uptime percentage.

availabilityThresholdSettingsLimits.description: Threshold limits for a single availability category. Status classification: value >= okLimit = Good, value >= goodLimit = Ok, value < goodLimit = Poor.

goodLimit.description: Minimum percentage for 'Ok' status. Values >= goodLimit but < okLimit are 'Ok'. Must be > 0.

okLimit.description: Minimum percentage for 'Good' status. Values >= okLimit are 'Good'. Must be > goodLimit.

ApplianceBusinessHourConfig.description: Business hour configuration for a single appliance defining working hours (KPI Time Settings) for availability calculations. When iscustombusinesshour is false, 24/7 monitoring is used regardless of other settings.

iscustombusinesshour.description: Enable custom business hours. When false, availability is calculated 24/7 ignoring start/end hours.

businesshourstart.description: Business day start hour (24-hour format). Only applied when iscustombusinesshour is true.

businesshourend.description: Business day end hour (24-hour format). Only applied when iscustombusinesshour is true.

timezone.description: Timezone for interpreting business hours. Use Java TimeZone ID or 'Use appliance timezone' to inherit from appliance /datetime config.
timezone.x-validation: Must be valid Java TimeZone ID or literal 'Use appliance timezone'

ApplianceBusinessHourConfig.x-notes: Configurations are stored in ClickHouse database. Changes are logged via ActionManager system action log.

ApplianceIdsRequest.description: Request object containing appliance identifiers to query.

AvailabilityTimeSettingsGetResponse.description: Array of business hour configurations for the requested appliances.

AvailabilityTimeSettingsPostRequest.description: Array of business hour configurations to apply to appliances.

AvcModeAggregateResponse.description: AVC mode status aggregated across all appliances in the Orchestrator.

AVC.description: Aggregate AVC mode status indicating the distribution of appliance versions. Determined by comparing appliance versions against the 8.1.6 threshold.

x-enum-descriptions.all: All appliances are running version 8.1.6 or above and support enhanced AVC features.
x-enum-descriptions.none: No appliances support AVC mode (all are below version 8.1.6).
x-enum-descriptions.mixed: Some appliances support AVC (8.1.6+) while others do not (below 8.1.6).

AvcModeSingleResponse.description: AVC mode status for a single specified appliance.

AVC.description: AVC mode status for the specified appliance. Based on whether the appliance version is 8.1.6 or above.

x-enum-descriptions.new: Appliance is running version 8.1.6 or above and supports enhanced AVC features.
x-enum-descriptions.old: Appliance is running a version below 8.1.6 and does not support enhanced AVC features.

AWSCloudResourceItem.description: Individual AWS cloud resource with its Terraform resource name and AWS resource ID.

name.description: Terraform resource name identifying the resource type and purpose (e.g., 'vpc', 'internet-gateway', 'instance-1-ec2', 'security-group-mgmt').

id.description: AWS-assigned resource identifier (e.g., 'vpc-xxx', 'i-xxx', 'sg-xxx', 'eni-xxx', 'igw-xxx', 'eipalloc-xxx').

AWSCloudResourcesResponse.description: Response containing AWS cloud resources provisioned by Terraform for a deployment. Resources are categorized into common artifacts (shared across all instances) and per-instance artifacts.

commonArtifacts.description: List of AWS resources shared across all instances in the deployment (VPC, Internet Gateway, Security Groups, Route Tables, etc.).

perInstanceArtifacts.description: Map of instance-specific resources keyed by instance identifier (e.g., 'instance-1', 'instance-2'). Each instance contains its EC2 instance, ENIs, and Elastic IPs.

AWSDeploymentConfigRequest.description: Configuration for deploying EdgeConnect Cloud Hub appliances in AWS.

name.description: Unique deployment name. Alphanumeric and dash (-) only, max 20 characters.

accountId.description: UUID of a registered AWS account. Obtain from GET /cloudDeployment/aws/accounts.

provider.description: Cloud provider identifier. Must be 'aws' for AWS deployments.

region.description: AWS region for deployment (e.g., us-west-2, eu-west-1). Must be valid for the account.

vpcCidr.description: CIDR block for the new VPC (e.g., 10.100.0.0/16). Must be valid IPv4 CIDR notation.

sshKeyName.description: Name of an existing EC2 key pair in the target region for SSH access.

bandwidth.description: Expected WAN bandwidth in Mbps. Used to determine instance sizing.

boost.description: Enable WAN Optimization (Boost) capability on the appliance.

instanceType.description: AWS EC2 instance type (e.g., c5.large, c5.xlarge). Must support the requested bandwidth.

amiId.description: Custom AMI ID to use. If omitted, the latest EdgeConnect AMI from Cloud Portal is used.

numInstances.description: Number of appliances to deploy. Must equal the length of the instances array.

instances.description: Per-appliance configuration array. Length must match numInstances.

awsTags.description: Custom AWS resource tags as comma-separated key=value pairs.

comment.description: Optional description for the deployment.

AWSDeploymentConfigResponse.description: AWS Cloud Hub deployment configuration returned from GET requests.

id.description: Orchestrator-assigned unique deployment ID.

accountId.description: UUID of the AWS account used for this deployment.

provider.description: Cloud provider identifier. Always 'aws' for AWS deployments.

name.description: Unique deployment name.

bandwidth.description: Configured WAN bandwidth in Mbps or 'Unlimited'.

boost.description: Whether WAN Optimization (Boost) is enabled.

numInstances.description: Number of appliances in this deployment.

comment.description: Optional description for the deployment.

region.description: AWS region where appliances are deployed.

sshKeyName.description: EC2 key pair name used for SSH access.

vpcCidr.description: CIDR block of the deployment VPC.

amiId.description: AMI ID used for the deployment. May be null if using default.

awsTags.description: Custom AWS resource tags as comma-separated key=value pairs.

instances.description: Array of deployed appliance instances with network configuration.

AWSInstanceAddRequest.description: Request object for adding a new instance to an existing AWS Cloud Hub deployment.

availabilityZone.description: AWS availability zone for the new instance (e.g., us-west-2a, us-west-2b). Must be valid for the deployment's region.

tag.description: Unique appliance tag identifier for this instance. Alphanumeric and dash (-) only, max 25 characters. Must not conflict with existing instance tags in the deployment. Auto-generated if omitted.

AWSInstanceRequest.description: Configuration for a single AWS EdgeConnect instance within a deployment.

availabilityZone.description: AWS availability zone for this instance (e.g., us-west-2a). Must be valid for the deployment region.

tag.description: Unique appliance tag identifier. Alphanumeric and dash (-) only, max 25 characters. Auto-generated if omitted.

AWSInstanceResponse.description: AWS EdgeConnect instance details including network configuration assigned after deployment.

availabilityZone.description: AWS availability zone where instance is deployed.

tag.description: Unique appliance tag identifier.

bandwidth.description: Instance bandwidth in Kbps.

automateConfigDone.description: Whether automated configuration has been completed.

comment.description: Optional instance-level comment.

AccountConfig.description: AWS account configuration for cloud deployment operations. Contains credentials and metadata for authenticating with AWS services.

id.description: Orchestrator-assigned unique identifier (UUID) for this AWS account. Auto-generated on account creation; do not include in POST requests.

name.description: Unique display name for the AWS account. Used for identification in the UI and API responses. Must not conflict with existing account names.

accessKey.description: AWS IAM access key ID for API authentication. Typically starts with 'AKIA' for long-term credentials.

secretKey.description: AWS IAM secret access key paired with the access key. Encrypted before storage. Not returned in GET responses for security.

comment.description: Optional description or notes for the AWS account. Useful for documenting the account purpose or environment.
comment.example: Production AWS account for EdgeConnect deployments

AccountConfigResponse.description: AWS account configuration returned from GET requests. The secretKey is always empty for security.

id.description: Orchestrator-assigned unique identifier (UUID) for this AWS account.

name.description: Unique display name for the AWS account.

accessKey.description: AWS IAM access key ID for API authentication.

secretKey.description: Always returned as empty string for security. The actual secret is never exposed via the API.

comment.description: Optional description or notes for the AWS account.
comment.example: Production AWS account for EdgeConnect deployments

DeployStatusResponse.description: Response object containing GCP Cloud Hub deployment status information.

id.description: Orchestrator-assigned deployment ID.

name.description: Unique deployment name assigned during creation.

provider.description: Cloud provider identifier. Always 'gcp' for GCP deployments.

numInstances.description: Total number of Cloud Hub instances in this deployment.

status.description: Current deployment status code indicating the state of the deployment operation.

comment.description: User-provided description or notes for the deployment.

x-status-values.PENDING: 1 - Deployment is queued and waiting to start
x-status-values.DEPLOYING: 2 - Terraform apply is in progress, creating cloud resources
x-status-values.SUCCESS: 3 - Deployment completed successfully, all instances deployed
x-status-values.INCOMPLETE: 4 - Deployment finished with errors, check logs for details
x-status-values.DESTROYING: 5 - Terraform destroy is in progress, removing cloud resources

x-field-notes.status: Poll this field to monitor deployment progress. Values 3 or 4 indicate completion.
x-field-notes.numInstances: Reflects the total count, including instances being deployed or terminated.
x-field-notes.comment: May be null or empty if no comment was provided during deployment creation.

DeploymentConfigUpdate.description: Request payload for updating a GCP Cloud Hub deployment's comment/description field.

comment.description: Descriptive text for the deployment. Used for labeling, documentation, and organization. If null or empty, clears the existing comment.
comment.example: Production GCP Cloud Hub deployment - US region

x-behavior.nullHandling: If comment is null or empty, the deployment comment is set to an empty string
x-behavior.persistence: Comment is stored in the deployment configuration and persisted to the database

AzureCloudResource.description: Represents an Azure cloud resource deployed as part of the Route Server deployment.

name.description: Name of the Azure resource as defined in the deployment configuration.

id.description: Azure Resource Manager (ARM) resource ID. Uniquely identifies the resource in Azure.

AzureCloudResources.description: Azure cloud infrastructure resources created during EdgeConnect deployment.

commonArtifacts.description: Shared infrastructure resources used by all instances (VNets, NSGs, storage accounts). Excludes SSH keys.

perInstanceArtifacts.description: Instance-specific resources keyed by instance identifier (e.g., 'instance-1', 'instance-2').

AzureImage.description: Azure Marketplace image information for appliance deployment.

version.description: Image version. Use 'latest' for most recent.

AzureInstanceInfo.description: Configuration and status information for a deployed EdgeConnect NVA instance in Azure Virtual WAN hub. Contains network interface details, Azure-assigned IPs, and configuration status.

index.description: Instance index number (1-based). Identifies the instance within the deployment.

availabilityZone.description: Azure availability zone where the instance is deployed (e.g., '1', '2', '3').

tag.description: Unique EdgeConnect appliance tag for identification. Alphanumeric and dash allowed, max 25 chars.

bandwidth.description: Instance bandwidth capacity in Kbps as configured by the scale unit.

mgmt0PrivateIp.description: Azure-assigned private IP address for management interface (mgmt0).

mgmt0PublicIp.description: Azure-assigned public IP address for management interface (mgmt0). Used for Orchestrator connectivity.

wan0PrivateIp.description: Azure-assigned private IP address for WAN interface (wan0).

wan0PublicIp.description: Azure-assigned public IP address for WAN interface (wan0). Used for tunnel establishment.

lan0PrivateIp.description: Azure-assigned private IP address for LAN interface (lan0).

automateConfigDone.description: Indicates whether automated configuration has completed for this instance.

comment.description: Optional comment or description for this instance.

AzureInstanceObj.description: Configuration object for a new Azure EdgeConnect instance.

availabilityZone.description: Azure availability zone for the new instance. Required when deployment uses 'Availability Zone' option; ignored when using 'Availability Set' option.

tag.description: Unique appliance tag identifier for the new instance. Must be unique across all instances in the deployment. Used for identification and management purposes.

AzureLoadBalancerConfigArray.description: Array of Azure Internal Load Balancer deployment configurations. Returns empty array when no deployments exist.

AzureLoadBalancerConfigResponse.description: Azure Internal Load Balancer deployment configuration returned by GET endpoint. Contains all configuration properties with the Orchestrator-assigned ID.

id.description: Orchestrator-assigned unique deployment ID. Auto-generated on creation.

accountId.description: ID of the Azure account used for deployment.

provider.description: Cloud provider identifier. Always 'azure_load_balancer' for ILB deployments.

name.description: Unique deployment name. Alphanumeric, dash, and underscore allowed (max 20 chars).

bandwidth.description: Bandwidth allocation in Mbps or 'Unlimited'. Inherited from base config.

boost.description: Boost mode flag. Inherited from base config.

numInstances.description: Number of instances associated with this deployment.

comment.description: User-provided description or notes for the deployment.

resourceGroup.description: Azure resource group name containing the load balancer.

region.description: Azure region code where the load balancer is deployed.

vnetName.description: Azure Virtual Network name for the load balancer.

subnetId.description: Full Azure resource ID of the subnet. Present when using an existing subnet.

subnetIpMask.description: CIDR block for the subnet. Present when a new subnet was created during deployment.

frontendIpAddress.description: Static private IP address for the load balancer frontend. Required with existing subnet.

probePort.description: TCP port used for ILB health probes. Valid range: 1-65535.

AzureNVACloudResources.description: Azure NVA cloud resource information containing resource identifiers for the deployed Network Virtual Appliance.

nvaId.description: The Azure Resource Manager (ARM) resource ID of the deployed Network Virtual Appliance. This ID uniquely identifies the NVA instance within the Azure subscription.

AzureNVADeploymentConfigResponse.description: Azure NVA deployment configuration returned by GET operations. Contains all deployment settings and instance details.

id.description: Orchestrator-assigned unique deployment identifier.

provider.description: Cloud provider type. Always 'azure_nva' for Azure Virtual WAN NVA deployments.

name.description: Unique deployment name. Alphanumeric, dash, and underscore allowed, max 20 characters.

accountId.description: ID of the configured Azure cloud account in Orchestrator.

resourceGroup.description: Azure resource group name containing the Virtual WAN hub.

region.description: Azure region code where the Virtual WAN hub is deployed (e.g., eastus, westus2).

virtualHubId.description: Full Azure resource ID of the Virtual WAN hub.

virtualNetwork.description: Virtual network CIDR assigned to the Virtual WAN hub.

edgeConnectRelease.description: EdgeConnect software release version deployed on the instances.

scaleUnit.description: Azure NVA scale unit determining instance capacity and throughput.

edgeConnectASN.description: BGP Autonomous System Number assigned to EdgeConnect. Range: 64512-65534, excluding Azure reserved ASNs.

sshPublicKey.description: SSH public key configured for appliance access.

managedResourceGroupId.description: Azure managed resource group ID where NVA instances are deployed. Auto-generated.

nvaId.description: Azure Network Virtual Appliance resource ID. Populated after successful deployment.

numInstances.description: Number of EdgeConnect instances in this deployment (typically 2 for HA).

bandwidth.description: Bandwidth configuration in Mbps or 'Unlimited'.

boost.description: Indicates if boost mode is enabled for this deployment.

comment.description: User-defined comment or description for the deployment.
comment.example: Production deployment for East US region

instances.description: List of EdgeConnect instance configurations with network details. Empty array if instances not yet deployed.

DeployStatus.description: Deployment status enumeration for cloud deployments.

export_map.description:
Integer value of the 'Routes Export Policies' bitmask. Right now we have nine Route Export policies for each Peer Type namely
1) Locally configured,
2) Learned via subnet sharing,
3) Learned from a local BGP branch peer,
4) Learned from a local BGP branch-transit peer,
5)Learned from a local BGP PE router,
6)Remote BGP,
7) Remote BGP branch-transit peer, 8) Learned from a local OSPF peer,
9) Learned from a Remote OSPF peer.
These seven policies are represented with 9 binary values from right to left (1111111). We can turn on/off the policy by simple modifying respective binary value. For Example, to turn off export route policies 1 and 3 the bit map will look like 111111010. The equivalent decimal value for the bitmask is 506. So the rest API field should look like 'export_map': 506. Some of the predefined import_map values for the different Peer Types are {'Branch':511, 'Branch-transit':431 and 'PE-router':141}.By default we send a decimal value 4294967295 indicating the predefined bitmask of the Peer Type is not modified

DeploymentGet.description: Full deployment configuration for an appliance. To modify deployment settings, retrieve this object via GET /deployment, modify the needed fields, and POST the entire object to `POST /appliance/rest?nePk={nePk}&url=deployment`. **Common data paths:** Interfaces: `modeIfs[]` (each has `ifName` like 'lan0'/'wan0' and `applianceIPs[]`). DHCP server DNS: `modeIfs[].applianceIPs[].dhcpd.server.dns` (array of IP strings). Interface classification by label: `applianceIPs[].label` is a label ID string — look up names in `sysConfig.ifLabels.lan[]` or `sysConfig.ifLabels.wan[]`. Interface zone: `applianceIPs[].zone` is a zone ID number — look up names in `sysConfig.zones[]`. Interface VRF segment: `applianceIPs[].vrf` is a VRF ID number — look up names in `sysConfig.vrfs[]`.

modeIfs.description: All datapath interface configurations (LAN and WAN). Each entry represents one interface (e.g., lan0, wan0) and contains applianceIPs[] with IP addressing, DHCP server/relay settings, firewall harden level, label, zone, VRF, and NAT config. This is the primary array to iterate when modifying per-interface settings like DHCP DNS servers.

sysConfig.description: System configuration and lookup tables. Contains label, zone, VRF, and role name-to-ID mappings needed to resolve numeric IDs in modeIfs[].applianceIPs[] to human-readable names. For example, to find a 'Guest' zone: find the zone object in sysConfig.zones[] where name='Guest', then match its id against applianceIPs[].zone.

DeploymentPost.description: Deployment configuration object used for validation and for applying changes. This is the same structure returned by GET /deployment (minus read-only fields like scalars and mgmtIfData). To apply deployment changes to an appliance, POST this object to `POST /appliance/rest?nePk={nePk}&url=deployment` (see the 'appliance' tag). The entire deployment object must be sent — there is no partial update.

err.description: Deployment data validation result - OK: null, or in case of error, the error message here

FlowRecord.description:
A single flow record represented as a positional array with 78 fields. The actual API returns arrays, but this schema documents the field structure.

**Field Categories:**
- **Identity (0-2):** flowId, flowSeq, spId
- **Application (3, 40-41, 58):** application, serviceId, saasId, applicationType
- **Source Endpoint (4-10):** ip1 parts, ip1, port1
- **Destination Endpoint (11-17):** ip2 parts, ip2, port2
- **Traffic Stats (18-25):** status, reduction%, bytes, uptime
- **Routing (26-30, 60-62):** protocol, tunnels, VLAN, overlays, VRF
- **QoS (31-33, 50-53):** trafficClass, DSCP values
- **NAT (36-37, 54-57):** SNAT/DNAT addresses and ports
- **Timing (38-39, 42-43):** start/end time, slow flow detection
- **DNS (44-45):** resolved hostnames
- **Security (46-49, 59, 67-68):** zones, drop reasons, DDoS
- **Identity (63-66):** username, roles, device
- **VXLAN (69-70):** VNI Rx/Tx
- **Performance (71-74):** app delay metrics
- **Web Content (75-77):** reputation scores, category

flows.description:
Array of individual flow records. Each flow is returned as a positional array (not an object). See the FlowRecord schema for field documentation, or use the index mapping below.

**Flow Array Field Index:**

| Index | Field | Type | Description |
|-------|-------|------|-------------|
| 0 | flowId | int | Unique flow identifier |
| 1 | flowSeq | int | Flow sequence number |
| 2 | spId | int | Internal ID (reserved) |
| 3 | application | str | Application name (e.g., Https, ssh) |
| 9 | ip1 | str | Source IP address |
| 10 | port1 | int | Source port (0-65535) |
| 16 | ip2 | str | Destination IP address |
| 17 | port2 | int | Destination port (0-65535) |
| 18 | status | int | Optimization status code |
| 19 | reductionInbound | num | Inbound dedup % (0-100) |
| 24 | reductionOutbound | num | Outbound dedup % (0-100) |
| 25 | uptime | int | Flow duration (ms) |
| 26 | protocol | str | Network protocol (tcp/udp/icmp) |
| 27 | outboundTunnel | str | Outbound tunnel ID |
| 28 | inboundTunnel | str | Inbound tunnel ID |
| 31 | trafficClass | int | QoS class (1-10) |
| 38 | flowStartTime | int | Start timestamp (epoch ms) |
| 39 | flowEndTime | int | End timestamp (0 if active) |
| 46 | fromZone | int | Source security zone |
| 47 | toZone | int | Destination security zone |
| 58 | applicationType | str | Behavior type (Voice, Interactive, etc.) |
| 59 | dropReason | int | Drop code: 0=none, 1=ZBF, 2=Route, 3=IPS |
| 60 | overlayName | str | Overlay names |
| 61 | vrf1 | int | Source VRF/segment ID |
| 62 | vrf2 | int | Destination VRF/segment ID |

*See FlowRecord schema for complete 78-field reference including IP parts [4-8, 11-15], byte counters [20-23], DSCP [32-33, 50-53], NAT [36-37, 54-57], DNS [44-45], performance metrics [71-74], and web content [75-77].*
