passPhrase.description: Echo of the passphrase used for encrypted key decryption. Null if key was not encrypted.

isPFX.description: True if the validated certificate was in PFX/PKCS#12 format.

certKeyValidation.description: Request parameters for SSL certificate validation. Supports PEM and PFX/PKCS#12 formats with RSA or ECDSA keys.

certificateData.description: Base64-encoded X.509 certificate with data URI prefix. For PEM format, must contain '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----'. Supported algorithms: RSA, ECDSA with SHA256/SHA384/SHA512.

keyData.description: Base64-encoded private key with data URI prefix. Required for PEM certificates (not needed for PFX). Supports PKCS#1, PKCS#8, and EC private key formats.

intermediateCertFileContent.description: Base64-encoded intermediate CA certificate chain for establishing trust to root CA. Optional for validation.

password.description: Password for PFX/PKCS#12 file decryption. Required when isPFX is true.

passPhrase.description: Passphrase for encrypted PEM private keys. Required when keyData contains 'ENCRYPTED' marker.

isPFX.description: Set to true for PFX/PKCS#12 certificate bundles. When true, certificateData contains the complete bundle and keyData can be empty.

isSslCACert.description: Set to true for CA certificates. When true, private key validation is skipped.

isEncrypted.description: Indicates if the request payload uses client-side encryption with the randomizer field.

randomizer.description: Random string for client-side encryption. Required when isEncrypted is true.

AASLicenseDisplay.description: Display information for a single AAS-licensed feature. Used for UI presentation of license features. Data originates from Portal and is stored locally by OrchTokenManager.

name.description: Human-readable feature name for display in the UI. Examples: 'Overlay', 'Region', 'Hubs per Region', 'WAN Optimization'.

desc.description: Detailed description including feature limit information. Typically includes the feature name and its licensed limit.

enable.description: Whether this feature is enabled in the current license. When false, the feature exists but is not licensed for use.

token.description: Internal token key used to reference this feature in usage and validation endpoints. Typically ends with 'Limit' suffix (e.g., 'overlayLimit', 'regionLimit').

AASLicenseDisplayMap.description: Map of feature identifiers to their display information. Keys are short feature identifiers (e.g., 'overlay', 'region', 'hub') provided by Portal. Values contain display metadata for UI presentation. Data is stored unencrypted in gmsconfig database at /orchToken/display path.
AASLicenseDisplayMap.x-data-source: Populated by OrchTokenService from Portal AAS token response and stored via OrchTokenManager.saveToken()

AASLicenseStats.description: In-memory AAS licensing runtime statistics maintained by OrchTokenService. Stats are updated after each Portal poll (default: every 24 hours, or 5 minutes on retry after failure).

licenseTier.description: Current AAS license tier from Portal. Default: 'Unknown' before first successful poll.

expiry.description: AAS license expiration timestamp in epoch milliseconds. Default: 0 before first successful poll.

lastPollStatus.description: Status of the last AAS license poll attempt. Values: 'Unknown' (initial), 'Success', or 'Failed: <error message>'.

lastPoll.description: Timestamp of last poll attempt in epoch milliseconds. Default: 0 before first poll.

nextPoll.description: Scheduled timestamp for next poll in epoch milliseconds. Default: 0 before first poll. Interval is 24 hours on success, 5 minutes on failure.

AASLicenseTokenValidateHubMap.description: Map of appliance identifiers (nePk or discoveredId) to their proposed hub region configurations. Used to validate hub assignments against the AAS license limit for logical hubs per region before applying changes.
AASLicenseTokenValidateHubMap.x-key-format: Appliance identifier - either nePk (numeric string) or discoveredId for appliances not yet fully onboarded
x-validation-notes: Missing fields in LogicalHubRegion inherit current appliance configuration
All appliances in the request are validated together as a batch
Existing hub associations are temporarily removed before validating new configurations

AASLicenseTokenValidateMap.description: Map of feature keys (without 'Limit' suffix) to their requested values for validation. The 'Limit' suffix is appended automatically by the server (e.g., 'overlay' becomes 'overlayLimit'). Only the first numeric value in the 'value' array is used for validation.

AASLicenseUsage.description: Usage information for a single AAS-enforced feature. Contains the feature's display name, current usage count, and licensed limit. When used > limit, the feature is out of compliance.

name.description: Human-readable display name of the licensed feature (e.g., 'Overlay', 'Region', 'Hubs per Region').

used.description: Current usage count for this feature. Calculated based on active configurations in the system.

limit.description: Maximum allowed usage based on AAS license token. System limits apply for on-premise deployments without AAS tokens.

AASLicenseUsageMap.description: Map of AAS license token keys to their usage information. Keys are feature identifiers ending with 'Limit' (e.g., overlayLimit, regionLimit, hubLimit). Only features with enabled AAS license enforcement are included.
AASLicenseUsageMap.x-token-key-format: Feature token keys follow the pattern: <featureName>Limit

AASLicenseVal.description: Requested value for AAS license feature validation

value.description: Array containing the requested value(s) for the feature. Typically contains a single numeric value.

AASLicenseValidationResponse.description: Response map containing validation results for each requested feature. Keys match the request feature keys (without 'Limit' suffix). Each feature returns its requested value and a message indicating validation result.

region.message: Region usage has reached or exceeded the AAS license limit.

AASLicenseValidationResult.description: Validation result for a single feature. Contains the requested value and a message indicating whether the validation passed or failed.

value.description: The requested value(s) that were validated. Echo of the input value array.

message.description: Validation result message. Empty string indicates validation passed (within limit). Non-empty string contains error message when validation failed.
x-possible-values: {featureName} usage has reached or exceeded the AAS license limit.
{featureName} usage has reached or exceeded the system limit.
Unable to check AAS license limit as feature token key was unrecognized or not provided.

HubValidationResponse.description: Response from hub validation endpoint. Empty object indicates success; presence of 'message' field indicates validation failure.

message.description: Validation error message when hub limit is exceeded. Absent or empty when validation passes. Format: '<limit type> message. Unable to modify hub appliance in region <regionName>'
message.example: Hubs per Region usage has reached or exceeded the AAS license limit. Unable to modify hub appliance in region US-West

x-response-patterns.success: Empty object {} indicates all hub configurations are within license limits
x-response-patterns.failure: Object with 'message' field containing the error reason and affected region name

LicenseInfoByGet.description: Complete license information returned by GET /gmsLicense

availableAppliances.description: Number of appliance licenses still available (maxAppliances - usedAppliances)

code.description: Operation result code. 0 indicates success, -1 indicates license decryption/validation failure.

daysToExpiration.description: Days until license expires. Returns -999999 for indefinite/non-expiring licenses, -1 if already expired, or positive integer for days remaining.

expirationDate.description: License expiration date as epoch timestamp in milliseconds. Returns 0 for indefinite licenses or when no expiration is set.

licenseKey.description: The encrypted license key string currently stored on the Orchestrator

maxAppliances.description: Maximum number of appliances this license allows managing. Portal-based licenses may show 1000000 for unlimited.

message.description: Status message. Empty string on success, error description on failure.

serialNumber.description: Orchestrator serial number in format XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX (MAC address format). Default is 00-00-00-00-00-00 for virtual instances before license assignment.

usedAppliances.description: Number of appliances currently being managed

portalBasedExpiration.description: Expiration date from portal-based licensing (if applicable) as epoch timestamp in milliseconds

gmsLicenseBasedExpiration.description: Expiration date from traditional license key (if applicable) as epoch timestamp in milliseconds

LicenseInfoByPost.description: License information returned after applying a new license key via POST. Combines the 'rc' field (operation result) with full license details from getLicenseInfo().

rc.description: Return code for the POST operation. 0=license applied successfully, -1=exception during setLicenseInfo(). This is the primary indicator of operation success.

code.description: License decryption/validation result from getLicenseInfo(). 0=valid license, -1=license validation failure or no valid license.

message.description: Operation result message. On success: 'License key successfully applied'. On failure: specific error message such as 'License Key required', 'Bad license key', 'License key does not match this server', or 'This GMS license has expired on: <date>'.
message.example: License key successfully applied

licenseKey.description: The encrypted license key that was applied. Empty string if operation failed.

serialNumber.description: Orchestrator serial number in XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX format (MAC address). For virtual appliances, this is extracted from the license key. For physical appliances, this is the server's MAC address.

maxAppliances.description: Maximum number of appliances this license allows managing. Value is extracted from the license key and may increase if the new license allows more appliances than before.

usedAppliances.description: Number of appliances currently being managed by the Orchestrator.

availableAppliances.description: Number of appliance licenses still available (maxAppliances - usedAppliances).

expirationDate.description: License expiration date as epoch timestamp in milliseconds. Returns 0 for indefinite/non-expiring licenses. The effective expiration is the later of portalBasedExpiration and gmsLicenseBasedExpiration.

daysToExpiration.description: Days until license expires. Returns -999999 for indefinite/non-expiring licenses, -1 if already expired, or positive integer for days remaining.

portalBasedExpiration.description: Expiration date from portal-based licensing (ECSP/metered/CPX/EC) as epoch timestamp in milliseconds. Null if not using portal-based licensing.

gmsLicenseBasedExpiration.description: Expiration date from the traditional license key as epoch timestamp in milliseconds. Null for indefinite licenses or when no date is encoded in the key.

LicenseInfoByValidate.description: License key validation result returned by GET /gmsLicense/validation. Contains extracted details from the validated key including serial number and max appliances count.

code.description: Validation result code. 0=key is valid and can be applied, -1=validation failed (see message for details).

licenseKey.description: The currently stored license key on the Orchestrator (not the key being validated). Returned for reference only.

maxAppliances.description: Maximum appliances allowed by the validated license key. Extracted from the second field of the decrypted key (SERIAL#MAX[#DATE]).

message.description: Validation status message. Empty string on success. On failure: 'Bad license key' (decryption/format error) or 'License key does not match this server' (physical appliance serial mismatch).

serialNumber.description: Serial number extracted from the validated license key. Format: XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX (six pairs of ASCII characters separated by dashes, 17 characters total).

LicenseKey.description: Request body for setting a new license key

licenseKey.description: Encrypted license key string to apply. The key contains encoded serial number, max appliances, and optional expiration date.

LogicalHubRegion.description: Appliance configuration for logical hub per region AAS license validation. Defines site name, network role, and region assignment for hub counting.

site.description: Site name for the appliance. Hubs with the same site name in a region count as one logical hub. Empty or null site names cause each hub to count individually.

networkRole.description: Network role identifier determining if appliance counts as a hub. 0=SPOKE (not a hub), 1=HUB (counts toward limit), 3=NRHUB (counts toward limit). Values 2, 4, 5 are legacy/unused.

regionId.description: Overlay region identifier. Each region has its own hub limit. Default region (0) has no limit enforcement.

x-hub-counting-rules.sameSiteGrouping: Multiple hubs with identical non-empty site names in the same region count as 1 logical hub
x-hub-counting-rules.emptySiteIndividual: Hubs with empty/null site names each count as separate logical hubs
x-hub-counting-rules.defaultRegionNoLimit: Region 0 (Default) has no hub limit enforcement

PermissionResponse.description: Response object containing the user's permission level.

permission.description: The permission level of the user. 'rw' indicates read-write access (full permissions), 'r' indicates read-only access.

secondaryPort.description: Port number of the secondary RADIUS server. Required if secondaryHost is specified. In container mode, must be 1812.

type.description: Authentication protocol type. PAP (Password Authentication Protocol) or CHAP (Challenge-Handshake).

defaultRole.description: Default role assigned to RADIUS-authenticated users without specific role mapping.

samlAllObject.description: Map of SAML identity provider configurations. Keys are integer configuration IDs, values are SAML configuration objects.

samlConfig.description: SAML 2.0 identity provider configuration for single sign-on authentication.

name.description: Display name for this SAML configuration. Must be alphanumeric.

issuer.description: SAML issuer identifier, typically the identity provider's entity ID.

spEntityId.description: Service Provider (SP) entity identifier for this Orchestrator instance.

spAssertionConsumerServiceUrl.description: Service Provider Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL where SAML responses are posted.

idpSingleSignOnServiceUrl.description: Identity Provider Single Sign-On service URL for SAML authentication requests.

idpSingleLogoutServiceUrl.description: Identity Provider Single Logout service URL. Optional.

spSingleLogoutServiceUrl.description: Service Provider Single Logout service URL. Optional.

idpX509cert.description: Identity Provider X.509 certificate for signature verification. Always returned as empty string in GET responses for security.

spX509cert.description: Service Provider X.509 certificate for signing requests. Always returned as empty string in GET responses for security.

usernameAttr.description: SAML attribute containing the username. Often a standard claim URI.

rolesAttr.description: SAML attribute containing user roles for RBAC mapping.

applianceAccessGroupAttr.description: SAML attribute for RBAC appliance access group mapping. Optional.

defaultRole.description: Default RBAC role for SAML authenticated users when no specific role mapping exists.

authn_Request.description: Whether to include AuthnRequest in SAML authentication flow.

samlObject.description: SAML server configuration containing IdP and SP settings for SSO authentication.

name.description: Unique alphanumeric name for the SAML server configuration. Must contain only letters and numbers.

issuer.description: Identity Provider issuer URL used to identify the IdP in SAML assertions.

idpEntityId.description: Unique identifier (Entity ID) of the Identity Provider. Often the same as the issuer URL.

spEntityId.description: Unique identifier (Entity ID) of the Service Provider (Orchestrator). Used by the IdP to identify this application.

spAssertionConsumerServiceUrl.description: Service Provider endpoint URL that receives and processes SAML assertions from the IdP.

idpSingleSignOnServiceUrl.description: Identity Provider SSO URL where authentication requests are sent.

idpSingleLogoutServiceUrl.description: Identity Provider SLO URL for processing SP-initiated logout requests. Optional field.

spSingleLogoutServiceUrl.description: Service Provider endpoint for processing IdP-initiated logout requests. Optional field.

idpX509cert.description: IdP X.509 certificate in PEM format for signature validation. Required for POST, returned empty in GET responses for security.

spX509cert.description: Service Provider X.509 certificate in PEM format. Returned empty in GET responses for security.

usernameAttr.description: SAML assertion attribute name that contains the username. Maps IdP user identifier to Orchestrator username.

rolesAttr.description: SAML assertion attribute name containing RBAC roles. Maps IdP group/role to Orchestrator permissions.

applianceAccessGroupAttr.description: SAML assertion attribute name for appliance access group assignment. Controls which appliances the user can access.

defaultRole.description: Default Orchestrator role assigned to SAML users when no specific role mapping exists. Overridden by explicit role assignments.

authn_Request.description: When true, sends a signed AuthnRequest to the IdP. Default is false.

tacacsObject.description: TACACS+ server configuration for terminal access controller authentication.

primaryHost.description: Primary TACACS+ server hostname or IP address.

primaryKey.description: Primary server shared secret key. Always returned as empty string in GET responses for security.

primaryPort.description: Primary TACACS+ server port. Standard TACACS+ port is 49.

secondaryHost.description: Secondary (failover) TACACS+ server hostname or IP address. Optional.

secondaryKey.description: Secondary server shared secret key. Always returned as empty string in GET responses for security.

secondaryPort.description: Secondary TACACS+ server port. Only required if secondaryHost is configured.

type.description: TACACS+ authentication type. Valid values are 'PAP' (Password Authentication Protocol) or 'CHAP' (Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol).

defaultRole.description: Default RBAC role for TACACS+ authenticated users when no specific role mapping exists.

tacacsPostRequestObject.description: TACACS+ server configuration object for creating or updating remote authentication settings.

primaryHost.description: Hostname or IP address of the primary TACACS+ server. Must be a valid resolvable hostname or IPv4/IPv6 address.

primaryPort.description: Port number for the primary TACACS+ server. Standard TACACS+ port is 49. In container mode, must be exactly 49.

primaryKey.description: Shared secret key for primary server authentication. Required on first creation; can be omitted on update to keep existing key.

secondaryHost.description: Hostname or IP address of the backup TACACS+ server for failover. Optional; when provided, secondaryPort and secondaryKey become required.

secondaryPort.description: Port number for the secondary TACACS+ server. Required when secondaryHost is specified. In container mode, must be exactly 49.

secondaryKey.description: Shared secret key for secondary server authentication. Required when secondaryHost is specified on first configuration; can be omitted on update to keep existing key.

type.description: Authentication protocol type. PAP (Password Authentication Protocol) sends passwords in clear text. CHAP (Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol) uses challenge-response for improved security.

defaultRole.description: Default role assigned to users authenticated via TACACS+ when no role attribute is returned from the server. Common values: network-read, admin.

x-validation-rules.primaryHost: Must be a valid resolvable hostname or IP address
x-validation-rules.primaryKey: Required on first creation; cannot be empty if no existing configuration
x-validation-rules.secondaryKey: Required when secondaryHost is provided on first configuration
x-validation-rules.containerMode: In container mode, primaryPort and secondaryPort must be 49

SMTP.description: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) server configuration for email notifications.

server.description: SMTP server hostname or IP address (e.g., smtp.example.com).

emailSender.description: Email address used as the sender (From address) for outgoing emails.

emailSsl.description: Enable SSL/TLS encryption for SMTP connections. When true, default port is 465; when false, default port is 25.

emailAuthentication.description: Enable SMTP authentication. When true, userID and password are required.

userID.description: Username for SMTP server authentication. Required when emailAuthentication is true.

password.description: Password for SMTP server authentication. Always null in GET responses for security.

smtpPort.description: SMTP server port number. Default is 25 for non-SSL, 465 for SSL connections.

requireEmailVerification.description: Require email address verification before sending notifications. Defaults to true if not specified.

SMTPGetResponse.description: Response containing SMTP configuration and validation status. Empty object if no configuration exists.

isValidSMTPServer.description: Indicates if the configured SMTP server is valid and reachable.

smtp.description: Current SMTP server configuration. Password is always null for security.

SMTPRequest.description: Request body for configuring SMTP server settings. Uses alternate property names for JSON serialization.

emailServer.description: SMTP server hostname or IP address. Maps to 'server' field internally.

emailSender.description: Email address used as sender (From address) for outgoing emails.

emailSsl.description: Enable SSL/TLS encryption. When true, port defaults to 465; when false, defaults to 25.

emailAuthentication.description: Enable SMTP authentication. When true, emailUser and emailPassword are required.

emailUser.description: Username for SMTP authentication. Required when emailAuthentication is true.

emailPassword.description: Password for SMTP authentication. Required when emailAuthentication is true.

smtpPort.description: SMTP server port. If 0 or omitted, defaults to 25 (non-SSL) or 465 (SSL).

requireEmailVerification.description: Require email verification before sending notifications. Defaults to true if not specified.

SMTPTest.description: Legacy request object for sending a test email. Use SMTPTestRequest instead.

emailRecepients.description: Email address to send the test email to.

smtp.description: SMTP configuration to use for sending the test email.

SMTPTestRequest.description: Request object for sending a test email to verify SMTP configuration. Use 'recipients' for comma-separated email addresses and 'emailInfo' for SMTP settings.

recipients.description: Email address(es) to send the test email to. Multiple addresses can be comma-separated.

emailInfo.description: SMTP server configuration for sending the test email. Server, emailSender, and emailUser (if authentication enabled) are required.

DiskSpaceFullResponse.description: Response object containing disk space full notification status. When disk usage exceeds 90%, the WatchDog service automatically sets this flag and pauses stats collection.

isDisk90PercentFull.description: Indicates whether disk usage on /home partition exceeds 90%. When true, stats collection is paused.

isDismissed.description: User dismissal flag for the disk space warning notification. Only present when isDisk90PercentFull is true.

description.description: Human-readable message describing the disk space status with current usage percentage.
description.example: Disk space is extremely low (92% full). Stats collection will be paused until sufficient disk space is available.

example.description: Disk space is extremely low (92% full). Stats collection will be paused until sufficient disk space is available.

DiskSpaceInfo.description: Request object for updating disk space notification dismissal state. Stored in database as JSON via GmsConfigManager.

isDismissed.description: Set to true to dismiss the disk space warning notification in the UI. Default is false.

description.description: Human-readable description of the disk space status or reason for dismissal.
description.example: Disk space is extremely low (92% full). Stats collection will be paused until sufficient disk space is available.

GmsBriefInfo.description: Brief server status information including uptime, version, time, and operational modes. Useful for quick health checks and dashboard displays.

uptime.description: Human-readable duration since the Orchestrator server was started. Computed from server start time using SPUtil.uptime().

release.description: Current Orchestrator software release version number (VP_RELEASE_NUM). Format: major.minor.patch.build.

time.description: Current server timestamp formatted as 'd-MMM-yy HH:mm:ss z'. Reflects the server's local time and timezone.

timeZone.description: Server timezone identifier (e.g., 'UTC', 'America/Los_Angeles'). Retrieved from the server's SimpleDateFormat timezone configuration.

inContainerMode.description: Indicates whether the Orchestrator is deployed in a containerized environment. Determined by GmsEnv.isInContainer().

inGlpMode.description: Indicates whether GLP (Global Licensing Platform) mode is enabled. Only true when both container mode is active and GLP licensing is enabled via GlpManager.

GmsPingInfo.description: Orchestrator server health check response containing liveness status, version, uptime, and database connectivity. Used for load balancer health checks and monitoring.

message.description: Server liveness message. Always returns 'I am alive!' when the server is responding.
message.example: I am alive!

version.description: Current Orchestrator software version (VP_RELEASE_NUM). Format: major.minor.patch.build.

uptime.description: Human-readable duration since server started. Calculated from VistaPointServer.getServerStartTime().

time.description: Current server time in milliseconds since Unix epoch (January 1, 1970 UTC).

timeStr.description: Current server time as human-readable string using Java Date.toString() format.

hostname.description: Network hostname of the Orchestrator server. Retrieved via IPUtil.getHostname().

dbHealth.description: Database connectivity status. True if database health check query succeeds (returns > 0), false otherwise. Critical for determining full system health.

example.message: I am alive!

GmsServerInfo.description: Comprehensive Orchestrator server information including system specs, storage, network identity, and portal registration. Several infrastructure-related fields are returned only for non-container deployments and are omitted from responses when running in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

release.description: Orchestrator software release version (VP_RELEASE_NAME). Format: major.minor.patch.build.

serverStartTime.description: Server start timestamp in milliseconds since Unix epoch. Used to calculate uptime.

uptime.description: Human-readable duration since server started. Computed dynamically from serverStartTime via SPUtil.uptime().

numActiveUsers.description: Count of currently active user sessions on the Orchestrator. Retrieved from WebUserSessions.

hostName.description: Network hostname of the Orchestrator server. Retrieved via IPUtil.getHostname().

host.description: Default IP address or DNS name for GMS registration. Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

time.description: Current server time in milliseconds since Unix epoch. Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

serialNumber.description: Orchestrator license serial number. Retrieved from GmsLicensing.

domain.description: Domain name of the server. Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

osRev.description: Operating system kernel version (Linux) or 'Windows'. Retrieved via 'uname -r' on Unix systems. Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

memSize.description: Total system memory in kilobytes. Retrieved via 'free -k' on Linux, 0 on Windows. Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

numCpus.description: Number of available processor cores. Retrieved via Runtime.availableProcessors(). Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

model.description: Orchestrator hardware/virtual appliance model (e.g., 'EC-V', 'GX-V'). Retrieved from gmsConfig database.

platform.description: Deployment platform type (e.g., 'KVM', 'VMware', 'Docker', 'unknown'). Retrieved from platform.conf or gmsConfig.

hwRev.description: Hardware revision identifier. Shows board revision for physical appliances, 'PC' for Windows. Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

usedDiskSpace.description: Used disk space with 'KB' suffix. Retrieved via WatchDog.getDiskInfo(). 'Unknown' on Windows or errors. Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

freeDiskSpace.description: Available disk space with 'KB' suffix. Retrieved via WatchDog.getDiskInfo(). 'Unknown' on Windows or errors. Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

loadAverage.description: System load averages (1, 5, 15 min) from 'uptime' command. 'Unknown' on Windows. Returned only for non-container deployments and omitted from responses in container/cloud (DOCKER) deployments.

portalObjectId.description: Cloud Portal object identifier for this Orchestrator. Null if not registered with portal.

portalRegistrationUuid.description: UUID used for Cloud Portal registration. Retrieved from GmsUuidManager.

RootPasswordInfo.description: Root password change status object stored in the Orchestrator database. Used to track whether the default root password has been changed for security compliance.

passwordChanged.description: Indicates whether the default root password has been changed. True means password was updated from default, false means still using default password.

VersionInfo.description: Contains the current orchestrator version and list of all installed versions

current.description: Currently running orchestrator software version number (VP_RELEASE_NUM)

installed.description: List of all installed orchestrator versions found in /home/gms directories matching gms.X.X.X.X pattern

statsCollection.description: Configuration object controlling which statistics types are collected by the Orchestrator.

Tunnel.description: Enable/disable collection of tunnel statistics (bandwidth, latency, packet counts).

Flow.description: Enable/disable collection of network flow statistics.

Drops.description: Enable/disable collection of packet drop statistics.

Port.description: Enable/disable collection of port-level traffic statistics.

Jitter.description: Enable/disable collection of network jitter measurements.

Interface.description: Enable/disable collection of network interface statistics.

Dscp.description: Enable/disable collection of DSCP (Differentiated Services Code Point) statistics.

Dns.description: Enable/disable collection of DNS query and response statistics.

Drc.description: Enable/disable collection of Dynamic Rate Control statistics.

Shaper.description: Enable/disable collection of traffic shaper statistics.

TopTalkers.description: Enable/disable collection of top talkers (highest bandwidth consumers) statistics.

TrafficClass.description: Enable/disable collection of traffic classification statistics.

Behavioral.description: Enable/disable collection of behavioral analytics statistics.

InterfaceByOverlay.description: Enable/disable collection of interface statistics grouped by overlay.

mos.description: Enable/disable collection of Mean Opinion Score (MOS) statistics for voice quality.

securityPolicy.description: Enable/disable collection of security policy statistics.

GMSTreeConfigGet.description: User-specific GMS Tree Display settings. The object contains a single dynamic property whose name is the current username.

showAppliances.description: Controls tree view layout. "1" = flat tree view, "2" = nested tree view.

defaultOrganize.description: Appliance grouping mode. "1" = group by Regions; "2" = group by Group.

sort.description: Sorting mode. "1" = sort by IP numbers; "2" = sort by hostname.

GMSWizardGet.description: Configuration object for the Orchestrator Getting Started Wizard. Stored in the GMS config database.

autoOpen.description: Controls wizard auto-display on user login. Primitive boolean defaults to false if not specified.

GRNode.description: Represents a graphical node on the topology map, used to store position information for appliances and groups.

id.description: Unique identifier assigned by Orchestrator (format: '<index>.GrNode', e.g., '1.GrNode').

groupId.description: ID of the parent group this node belongs to (format: '<index>.Network', e.g., '10.Network').

sourceId.description: Source entity ID. For appliances: neId format '<index>.NE'. For groups: group ID format '<index>.Network'.

appliance.description: Computed field indicating node type. True for appliances, false for groups. Determined by checking if sourceId contains '.Network'.

wx.description: X-coordinate position in the map window (pixels). Value of -1 indicates unset position.

wy.description: Y-coordinate position in the map window (pixels). Value of -1 indicates unset position.

latitude.description: Geographic latitude coordinate. Value of 0 indicates unset location.

longitude.description: Geographic longitude coordinate. Value of 0 indicates unset location.

Group.description: Represents a group in the Orchestrator network hierarchy

id.description: Unique primary key for the group in format '{number}.Network'.

name.description: Unique display name of the group.

subType.description: Group type indicator: 0=Root Group, 2=Auto-discovered Group, 3=User-defined Group.

parentId.description: Primary key of the parent group. Null for the root group (0.Network).

backgroundImage.description: Filename of the background image/icon for the group.

GroupNewPostBody.description: Request body for creating a new group in the Orchestrator hierarchy

name.description: Unique display name for the group. Must be non-empty and unique across all groups.

parentId.description: Primary key of the parent group in format '{number}.Network'. Defaults to '0.Network' (root group) if omitted. Cannot be '2.Network' (auto-discovered group).

backgroundImage.description: Filename of the background image/icon for the group. Defaults to 'data_net.png' if omitted.

GroupUpdatePostBody.description: Request body for updating an existing user-defined group

id.description: Primary key of the group to update in format '{number}.Network'. Only user-defined groups (id >= 3.Network) can be updated.

name.description: New unique display name for the group. Must be non-empty.

backgroundImage.description: Optional new background image/icon filename for the group.

RootGroup.description: Represents the root group (0.Network) in the Orchestrator hierarchy. The root group is the top-level container for all network groups and is a system group that cannot be modified or deleted.

id.description: Unique identifier for the root group. Always '0.Network'.

name.description: Display name of the root group. Typically 'Network'.

subType.description: Group type indicator. Always 0 for the root group.

parentId.description: Parent group ID. Always null for the root group as it has no parent.

backgroundImage.description: Filename of the background image/icon for the root group.

name.description: Name of the template group

selectedTemplates.description: All selected template(s) data in the template group

templates.description: All templates data in the template group

HaGroupsRequest.description: Request payload for saving HA groups. Map where keys are numeric group IDs (as strings starting from '0') and values are HAGroup objects. This replaces the entire HA groups configuration.

HaGroupsResponse.description: Response containing all HA groups. Map where keys are numeric group IDs (as strings) and values are HAGroup objects. Returns empty object {} if no HA groups configured.

AlarmPeriodSummary.description: Summary of alarms for an appliance within a specified time period. Contains the most recent alarm for each severity level and counts of all alarms by severity.

critical.description: Most recent critical severity alarm in the time period, or null if none exist

major.description: Most recent major severity alarm in the time period, or null if none exist

minor.description: Most recent minor severity alarm in the time period, or null if none exist

warning.description: Most recent warning severity alarm in the time period, or null if none exist

alarmCountsInPeriod.description: Map of alarm severity to count for all alarms (active and closed) within the time period

AlarmPeriodSummaryItem.description: Details of the most recent alarm for a specific severity level within the queried time period

sequenceId.description: Unique alarm sequence identifier assigned by the system

description.description: Human-readable description of the alarm condition

time.description: Timestamp when the alarm was created in milliseconds since EPOCH

BwUtilizationThreshold.description: Bandwidth utilization threshold settings as percentage values (0-100).

goodLimit.description: Upper boundary for healthy bandwidth utilization (percentage). Values at or below this are healthy.

okLimit.description: Upper boundary for warning bandwidth utilization (percentage). Values above this are critical.

CountSummary.description: Count of alarms by severity level within the queried time period

HealthFetchParams.description: Parameters for fetching health summary data for appliances over a specified time range

from.description: Start time in seconds since EPOCH (Unix timestamp). Defines the beginning of the data time range.

to.description: End time in seconds since EPOCH (Unix timestamp). Defines the end of the data time range.

overlayId.description: Overlay ID to filter results. Use -1 to query all overlays.

verticals.description: List of health metric types to include in the response.

from.description: Long(Signed 64 bits) value of seconds since EPOCH time indicating the starting time boundary of data time range

to.description: Long(Signed 64 bits) value of seconds since EPOCH time indicating the ending time boundary of data time range

HealthSummaryResp.description: Health summary response containing hourly health entries organized by appliance ID. Keys are appliance IDs (nePks) and values are arrays of hourly health entries.

additionalProperties.description: Array of hourly health status entries for the appliance, ordered by time

HealthVertical.description: Health metric categories for monitoring appliance and network health

x-enum-descriptions.MOS: Mean Opinion Score for voice quality (overlay-affected)

JitterPeriodSummary.description: Jitter health metrics summary for the worst-performing tunnel during the specified time period. Includes time spent in each health state and maximum observed jitter value.

criticalMins.description: Minutes spent in critical jitter state during the period. Critical threshold is defined by health configuration.

majorMins.description: Minutes spent in major jitter state during the period. Major threshold is defined by health configuration.

normalMins.description: Minutes spent in normal/healthy jitter state during the period.

max.description: Maximum jitter value observed during the period in milliseconds.

tunnelId.description: Name of the tunnel with the worst jitter performance during the period.

healthStatus.description: Overall health status for jitter during the period. Determined by worst-case minutes (critical > major > healthy).

x-enum-descriptions.HEALTHY: Jitter within normal thresholds throughout the period
x-enum-descriptions.MAJOR: Jitter exceeded major threshold for some minutes
x-enum-descriptions.CRITICAL: Jitter exceeded critical threshold for some minutes

JitterThreshold.description: Network jitter threshold settings in milliseconds.

goodLimit.description: Upper boundary for healthy jitter (ms). Values at or below this are healthy.

okLimit.description: Upper boundary for warning jitter (ms). Values above this are critical.

LatencyPeriodSummary.description: Latency health metrics summary for the worst-performing tunnel during the specified time period. Includes time spent in each health state and maximum observed latency value.

criticalMins.description: Minutes spent in critical latency state during the period. Critical threshold is defined by health configuration.

majorMins.description: Minutes spent in major latency state during the period. Major threshold is defined by health configuration.

normalMins.description: Minutes spent in normal/healthy latency state during the period.

max.description: Maximum latency value observed during the period in milliseconds.

tunnelId.description: Name of the tunnel with the worst latency performance during the period.

healthStatus.description: Overall health status for latency during the period. Determined by worst-case minutes (critical > major > healthy).

x-enum-descriptions.HEALTHY: Latency within normal thresholds throughout the period
x-enum-descriptions.MAJOR: Latency exceeded major threshold for some minutes
x-enum-descriptions.CRITICAL: Latency exceeded critical threshold for some minutes

LatencyThreshold.description: Network latency threshold settings in milliseconds.

goodLimit.description: Upper boundary for healthy latency (ms). Values at or below this are healthy.

okLimit.description: Upper boundary for warning latency (ms). Values above this are critical.

LossPeriodSummary.description: Packet loss health metrics summary for the worst-performing tunnel during the specified time period. Includes time spent in each health state and maximum observed loss percentage.

criticalMins.description: Minutes spent in critical loss state during the period. Critical threshold is defined by health configuration.

majorMins.description: Minutes spent in major loss state during the period. Major threshold is defined by health configuration.

normalMins.description: Minutes spent in normal/healthy loss state during the period.

maxLossPercentage.description: Maximum packet loss percentage observed during the period. Value is divided by 100 from raw data and rounded to 2 decimal places.

tunnelId.description: Name of the tunnel with the worst loss performance during the period.

healthStatus.description: Overall health status for packet loss during the period. Determined by worst-case minutes (critical > major > healthy).

x-enum-descriptions.HEALTHY: Loss within normal thresholds throughout the period
x-enum-descriptions.MAJOR: Loss exceeded major threshold for some minutes
x-enum-descriptions.CRITICAL: Loss exceeded critical threshold for some minutes

MosPeriodSummary.description: MOS (Mean Opinion Score) health metrics summary for the worst-performing tunnel during the specified time period. MOS measures voice quality on a scale of 1-5, where 5 is excellent and 1 is poor.

criticalMins.description: Minutes spent in critical MOS state during the period. Critical threshold is defined by health configuration (typically MOS < 1).

majorMins.description: Minutes spent in major MOS state during the period. Major threshold is defined by health configuration.

normalMins.description: Minutes spent in normal/healthy MOS state during the period (typically MOS >= 4).

tunnelId.description: Name of the tunnel with the worst MOS performance during the period.

healthStatus.description: Overall health status for MOS during the period. Determined by worst-case minutes (critical > major > healthy).

x-enum-descriptions.HEALTHY: MOS within normal thresholds throughout the period (typically >= 4)
x-enum-descriptions.MAJOR: MOS dropped below major threshold for some minutes
x-enum-descriptions.CRITICAL: MOS dropped below critical threshold for some minutes (typically < 1)

MosThreshold.description: Mean Opinion Score (MOS) threshold settings on a scale of 1-5. Note: For MOS, lower values indicate worse quality, so the threshold logic is inverted.

goodLimit.description: Lower boundary for critical MOS. Values at or below this are critical.

okLimit.description: Lower boundary for healthy MOS. Values at or above this are healthy.

PacketLossThreshold.description: Packet loss threshold settings as percentage values.

goodLimit.description: Upper boundary for healthy packet loss (percentage). Values at or below this are healthy.

okLimit.description: Upper boundary for warning packet loss (percentage). Values above this are critical.

alarmObj.description: Alarm severity toggle settings that control which alarm levels affect health status calculations.

critical.description: Include critical severity alarms in health calculations.

major.description: Include major severity alarms in health calculations.

minor.description: Include minor severity alarms in health calculations.

warning.description: Include warning severity alarms in health calculations.

appliance-Item.description: Hourly health status entry for an appliance representing aggregated health data

blank.description: True if no health data was collected for this hour (padding entry). When true, other fields may have default values.

configChange.description: True if a configuration change occurred during this hour

reboot.description: True if the appliance rebooted during this hour

status.description: Aggregated health status for the hour based on configured thresholds

time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds since EPOCH) representing the start of the hour boundary

healthThresholdConfig.description: Health threshold configuration defining boundaries for network health metrics. Values below goodLimit are considered healthy, values between goodLimit and okLimit are warnings, values above okLimit are critical.

alarm.description: Alarm severity toggles controlling which alarm levels affect health.

HostName.description: Response object containing the Orchestrator hostname

gms_hostname.description: Hostname or domain name of the Orchestrator. In container mode, returns the registered domain; otherwise returns the system hostname or 'localhost' as fallback.

HttpsCertificateResponse.description: HTTPS certificate configuration details from the appliance

serialNumber.description: Certificate serial number in hexadecimal format

ERROR.description: Error indicator when certificate is not available

IdsSignatureRule.description: Represents an individual IDS/IPS signature rule with its detection and action configuration.

id.description: Unique numeric identifier for the signature rule.

name.description: Human-readable name of the signature rule.

description.description: Detailed description of what the rule detects and its purpose.

action.description: Default action for the rule: 'drop' to block traffic, 'alert' for inspection only.

severity.description: Severity level of the threat detected by this rule.

affected_products.description: Comma-separated list of products or platforms affected by the threat.

signature_family.description: Signature family version this rule belongs to.

idpsAutoUpdateGet.description: Response object containing the IDPS auto signature update state.

auto.description: Current state of automatic signature updates. Returns 'on' when enabled, 'off' when disabled.

idpsAutoUpdatePut.description: Request body for updating IDPS auto signature update state.

auto.description: Set 'on' to enable or 'off' to disable auto updates. Case-insensitive; stored lowercase.

idpsAutoUpdatePutResponse.description: Response confirming the auto signature update state change.

auto.description: The submitted auto update value (case preserved from request).

idsConfigGet.description: IDS/IPS global configuration response containing schedule settings, supported appliances, and version information.

id.description: Unique database identifier for the configuration record.

resourceBase.description: Resource base path in the database. Always '/config' for global IDS configuration.

configData.description: Configuration data containing schedule, auto-update settings, appliance versions, and signatures.

schedule.description: Signature download schedule configuration. Supports various recurrence patterns.

effectiveTime.description: Schedule start time in Unix epoch seconds.

endTime.description: Optional schedule end time in Unix epoch seconds.

runNow.description: When true, triggers immediate signature download.

recurrence.description: Recurrence pattern: minutes, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.

auto.description: Auto-update state for IDS signatures. Valid values: 'on' or 'off'.

idsVersions.description: Map of appliance nePk identifiers to their current IDS signature versions.

IPSLAManagers.description: Manager object naming convention: The name of the manager object should look like '(MGR)_(operation type)_(max number)'. for example a manager with interface monitor should look like 'MGR_port-monitor_10'. Here port-monitor is the monitor type of the manager and the last number should be the unique and generally it should be the increment of the max number used across all the existing Manager,Operation and Action objects.

downAction.description:
Specify action rules to be executed when monitor is down .

Down Action object naming convention: The name of the down action object should be like '(DN_ACTION)_(down action type)_(max number)'.For example a down action for disabling tunnel should look like 'DN_ACTION_tun-dn_11'. Here tun-dn is the action type and the last number should be the unique and generally it should be the increment of the max number used across all the existing Manager, Operation and Action objects.

The following are the supported up action types and it's attributes.
Enable Tunnel
type :tun-up,
Attributes
tun-alias: Alias of the tunnel

Disable Tunnel
type :tun-dn,
Attributes
tun-alias: Alias of the tunnel

VRRP Priority
type :vrrp-prio,
Attributes
inc: Increment VRRP priority by X number or dec: Decrease VRRP priority
port-name: Name of the interface or port-label: Label of the interface

Advertise subnets to Silver Peak peers
type :subnet-adv,
Attributes
port-name: Name of the interface or port-label: Label of the interface

Disable Subnet Sharing
type :subnet-shar,
Attributes
No attributes for this action

Modify Subnet Metric
type :subnet-metric,
Attributes
delta: Add a metric delta to the metric of all subnets shared with Silver Peak peers

Remove Auto Subnet - Remove from the subnet table an auto subnet for a port (including all VLAN & subinterface subnets).
type :subnet-rmv,
Attributes
port-name: Name of the interface or port-label: Label of the interface

Raise Alarm only. It doesn't contains any type or attributes. Ex: downAction: "alarm"

enable.description: Flag to enable and disable manger rule

operation.description:
Specifies the operations or monitor rules to be performed.

Operation object naming convention: The name of the operation/monitor object should be like '(OPR)_(operation type)_(max number)'. For example an operation for monitoring interface should be like 'OPR_ip-monitor_11'. Here ip-monitor is the operation type and the last number should be the unique and generally it should be the increment of the max number used across all the existing Manager, Operation and Action objects.

The following are the supported monitor types and it's attributes.
Interface Monitor
type :port-monitor,
Attributes
port-name: Name of the interface to be monitored ex:lan0 or port-label: Name of the interface label to be monitored ex:MPLS

Ping Monitor

dn-thresh: Mark down after X number of failed pings

Attributes
port-name: Name of the interface to be monitored ex:lan0 or port-label: Name of the interface label to be monitored ex:MPLS

upAction.description:
Specify action rules to be executed when monitor is up .

Up Action object naming convention: The name of the up action object should be like '(UP_ACTION)_(up action type)_(max number)'. For example an up action for enabling tunnel should look like 'UP_ACTION_tun-up_11'. Here tun-up is the action type and the last number should be the unique and generally it should be the increment of the max number used across all the existing Manager, Operation and Action objects.

The following are the supported up action types and it's attributes.
Enable Tunnel
type :tun-up,
Attributes
tun-alias: Alias of the tunnel

Disable Tunnel
type :tun-dn,
Attributes
tun-alias: Alias of the tunnel

VRRP Priority
type :vrrp-prio,
Attributes
inc: Increment VRRP priority by X number or dec: Decrease VRRP priority
port-name: Name of the interface or port-label: Label of the interface

Default Actions: These are special actions which doesn't have any attributes or type. These should be specified as direct string literal instead an object. Ex "upAction": "def-subnet".The following are the available default actions.
def-subnet - This reverts whatever was the Down Action back to the normal state.
For example:
If Down Action is Disable Subnet Sharing, the Up Action is re-enable Subnet Sharing.
If Down Action is Remove Auto Subnets, the Up Action re-adds the auto subnet.
If Down Action is Modify Subnet Metric, the Up Action restores subnet metrics to their original value.
def-vrrpt - Reverts the VRRP priority back to the configured value.
def-alarm - Clears the alarm once the monitor is up.

up_threshold.description: Number of consecutive successful requests needed to change the state of the monitor to UP

dir.description: Traffic direction for NAT application. Required field.

gms_marked.description: Flag indicating if rule was created by Orchestrator ('true') or locally on appliance ('false').

match.description: Traffic matching criteria. All specified criteria must match for rule to apply.

proto.description: Protocol to match. 'any' matches all protocols.

dst_subnet.description: Destination IP subnet in CIDR notation. Use '0.0.0.0/0' to match any destination. Required if src_subnet is not specified.

trans_dport.description: Translated destination port or range. Must match dst_port format. Cannot overlap with dst_port. Empty string if not used.

gms_marked.description: Indicates if the rule was marked by Orchestrator.

InterfaceObj.description: OSPF configuration settings for a single interface

adminStatus.description: Administrative state of OSPF on this interface. True enables OSPF, false disables it.

area.description: OSPF area identifier in dotted decimal format (e.g., 0.0.0.0 for backbone area).

authType.description: Authentication type for OSPF packets. Use either plain text (Text) or MD5 authentication, not both.

authKey.description: Plain text authentication key. Used only when authType is 'Text'. Mutually exclusive with MD5 authentication.

md5Key.description: MD5 key identifier (1-255). Used only when authType is 'MD5'. Mutually exclusive with plain text authentication.

md5Password.description: MD5 authentication password. Used only when authType is 'MD5'. Mutually exclusive with plain text authentication.

bfdDesired.description: Enable BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) for faster failure detection on this interface.

cost.description: OSPF cost metric for the interface. Lower values indicate preferred paths.

deadInterval.description: Dead interval in seconds. Time without hello packets before declaring neighbor down. Typically 4x helloInterval.

helloInterval.description: Hello interval in seconds. Frequency of OSPF hello packets sent on this interface.

priority.description: Router priority for DR/BDR election. Higher values increase election priority. Zero prevents DR/BDR eligibility.

comment.description: Optional user-defined comment or note for this interface configuration.

InterfacesObj.description: Map of OSPF interface configurations within a VRF segment. Each key is the interface name (e.g., 'lan0', 'wan0').

InterfacesResponse.description: Map of interface names to their OSPF configuration. Keys are interface names (e.g., lan0, wan0).

MultiSegmentOSPFAreasConfig.description: Map of segment IDs to OSPF area configurations. Keys are segment ID strings. When segmentation is disabled, only segment '0' exists.

MultiSegmentOSPFConfig.description: Map of segment IDs to their OSPF system configurations. Keys are string segment identifiers (e.g., '0', '1'), values are OSPFSystemConfig objects.

MultiSegmentOSPFInterfaceState.description: OSPF interface state organized by segment ID. Each key is a segment identifier (numeric string).

MultiSegmentOSPFInterfacesConfig.description: Map of OSPF interface configurations organized by VRF segment ID. Each key represents a segment ID (routing instance), containing interface configurations for that segment.

MultiSegmentOSPFNeighborsState.description: OSPF neighbors state organized by VRF segment ID. Each key represents a segment identifier.

MultiSegmentOSPFState.description: Map of OSPF system state indexed by segment ID. Each key represents a VRF segment identifier (e.g., '0' for default segment).

OSPFAreaConfigObject.description: Configuration settings for a single OSPF area including area type and NSSA-specific options.

area_type.description: OSPF area type. 0 = Standard area, 1 = NSSA (Not-So-Stubby Area).

redist.description: NSSA external route redistribution. When true, router originates NSSA LSAs for external routes. When false, suppresses NSSA LSA generation. Only applicable for NSSA areas.

summary.description: Summary LSA import control for NSSA areas. When true, allows summary LSAs into NSSA. When false, blocks summary LSA origination and propagation.

translator_role.description: NSSA border router translator role for Type-7 to Type-5 LSA translation. 1 = Always translate, 2 = Candidate (elected), 3 = Never translate.

OSPFAreasConfig.description: Map of OSPF area IDs to their configuration objects. Keys are area IDs in dotted decimal notation (e.g., '0.0.0.0' for backbone area).

OSPFInterfaceStateResp.description: Response object containing an array of OSPF interface states.

interfaceState.description: List of OSPF-enabled interface states on the appliance.

OSPFNeighborsStateResp.description: Response object containing an array of OSPF neighbor states.

neighborState.description: List of OSPF neighbor state objects. Empty array if no neighbors are present.

OSPFStateObj.description: OSPF system state object containing routing protocol configuration and operational statistics.

router_id.description: OSPF router identifier, typically an IPv4 address format. Uniquely identifies this router within the OSPF domain.

ospf_enabled.description: Indicates whether OSPF routing is enabled on this appliance.

pm_admin_state.description: Process manager administrative state of the OSPF service (e.g., 'enabled', 'disabled').

proto_version.description: OSPF protocol version number. Typically 2 for OSPFv2 (IPv4) or 3 for OSPFv3 (IPv6).

num_nbrs.description: Total count of OSPF neighbors currently established with this router.

extnl_lsa_cnt.description: Number of external LSAs (Link State Advertisements) in the OSPF database.

extnl_lsa_refresh_intvl.description: Interval in seconds at which external LSAs are refreshed. Default is typically 1800 seconds (30 minutes).

hold_ls_intvl.description: Hold time interval in milliseconds between consecutive LSA transmissions for throttling.

max_ls_intvl.description: Maximum interval in milliseconds between LSA transmissions during throttling.

min_lsa_arrival.description: Minimum interval in milliseconds between accepting the same LSA from neighbors.

min_lsa_interval.description: Minimum interval in milliseconds between originating the same LSA.

originated_new_lsas.description: Cumulative count of new LSAs originated by this router since startup.

num_learned_extnl_ospf.description: Number of external routes learned via OSPF from other routers.

route_calc_max_delay.description: Maximum delay in milliseconds before SPF (Shortest Path First) route calculation starts.

redist_bgp.description: Enables redistribution of BGP routes into OSPF when true.

redist_bgp_metric.description: Metric value assigned to BGP routes redistributed into OSPF.

redist_bgp_route_tag.description: Route tag assigned to BGP routes redistributed into OSPF for filtering purposes.

redist_bgp_route_type.description: OSPF external route type for redistributed BGP routes. Value 1 = E1 (considers internal cost), 2 = E2 (ignores internal cost).

redist_local.description: Enables redistribution of local/connected routes into OSPF when true.

redist_local_metric.description: Metric value assigned to local routes redistributed into OSPF.

redist_local_route_tag.description: Route tag assigned to local routes redistributed into OSPF for filtering purposes.

redist_local_route_type.description: OSPF external route type for redistributed local routes. Value 1 = E1, 2 = E2.

redist_subshared.description: Enables redistribution of Silver Peak SD-WAN overlay routes into OSPF when true.

redist_subshared_metric.description: Metric value assigned to Silver Peak routes redistributed into OSPF.

redist_subshared_route_tag.description: Route tag assigned to Silver Peak routes redistributed into OSPF for filtering purposes.

redist_subshared_route_type.description: OSPF external route type for redistributed Silver Peak routes. Value 1 = E1, 2 = E2.

OSPFSystemConfig.description: OSPF system-level configuration object containing routing protocol settings and redistribution options.

enable.description: Enables or disables OSPF routing protocol on the appliance. When enabled, routerId cannot be 0.0.0.0.

routerId.description: OSPF router identifier in IPv4 format. Must be a valid IPv4 address; 0.0.0.0 is not allowed when OSPF is enabled.

opaque_enable.description: Enables opaque link-state advertisements (LSA Types 9, 10, 11) for OSPF. Used for extended OSPF capabilities like MPLS TE.

redistBgp.description: Enables redistribution of BGP routes into OSPF. When true, BGP learned routes are advertised via OSPF.

bgpRedistMetric.description: Metric value assigned to redistributed BGP routes. Range: 0-4294967295.

bgpRedistMetricType.description: OSPF external metric type for redistributed BGP routes. Value 1 = E1 (Type 1 External), Value 2 = E2 (Type 2 External). Default is E2.

bgpRedistTag.description: Route tag for redistributed BGP routes. Used for filtering and policy-based routing. Range: 0-4294967295.

redistLocal.description: Enables redistribution of local (connected) routes into OSPF. When true, directly connected networks are advertised.

localRedistMetric.description: Metric value assigned to redistributed local routes. Range: 0-4294967295.

localRedistMetricType.description: OSPF external metric type for redistributed local routes. Value 1 = E1 (Type 1 External), Value 2 = E2 (Type 2 External). Default is E2.

localRedistTag.description: Route tag for redistributed local routes. Used for filtering and policy-based routing. Range: 0-4294967295.

redistSubnetShare.description: Enables redistribution of Silver Peak (subnet sharing) routes into OSPF. Advertises SD-WAN fabric routes via OSPF.

subnetShareRedistMetric.description: Metric value assigned to redistributed Silver Peak routes. Range: 0-4294967295.

subnetShareRedistMetricType.description: OSPF external metric type for redistributed Silver Peak routes. Value 1 = E1 (Type 1 External), Value 2 = E2 (Type 2 External). Default is E2.

subnetShareRedistTag.description: Route tag for redistributed Silver Peak routes. Used for filtering and policy-based routing. Range: 0-4294967295.

interfaceStateObj.description: Represents the operational state of a single OSPF-enabled interface.

ifname.description: Interface name as configured on the appliance (e.g., lan0, wan0).

ip_addr.description: IP address assigned to this interface in dotted decimal notation.

area.description: OSPF area identifier in dotted decimal format. Area 0.0.0.0 is the backbone area.

interface_state.description: Current OSPF interface state. Possible values: Down, Loopback, Waiting, Point-to-Point, DR, Backup, DROther.

admin_status.description: Administrative status of OSPF on this interface (enabled or disabled).

ospf_if_type.description: OSPF network type for this interface. Determines adjacency formation and LSA flooding behavior.

desig_rtr.description: IP address of the Designated Router (DR) for this network segment. Only applicable on broadcast and NBMA networks.

bkup_desig_rtr.description: IP address of the Backup Designated Router (BDR) for this network segment.

hello_interval.description: Time in seconds between OSPF Hello packets. Must match all routers on the segment.

dead_interval.description: Time in seconds before a neighbor is declared dead if no Hello is received. Typically 4x hello_interval.

transmit_delay.description: Estimated time in seconds to transmit an LSA on this interface. Used in LSA age calculation.

rtr_priority.description: Router priority for DR/BDR election. Higher values increase election likelihood. Value of 0 makes router ineligible.

lsa_refresh_intvl.description: Interval in seconds at which self-originated LSAs are refreshed. Default is typically 1800 seconds (30 minutes).

if_max_bandwidth.description: Maximum interface bandwidth in bits per second. Used for OSPF cost calculation.

totalNeighbors.description: Total number of OSPF neighbors discovered on this interface, regardless of state.

activeNeighbors.description: Number of OSPF neighbors in Full adjacency state on this interface.

neighborStateObj.description: Represents the state of a single OSPF neighbor.

admin_status.description: Administrative status of the OSPF neighbor interface.

area.description: OSPF area ID in dotted decimal format that the neighbor belongs to.

dead_time.description: Remaining time in seconds before the neighbor is declared dead if no Hello packets are received.

desig_rtr_state.description: Designated Router election state of the neighbor.

hello_suppressed.description: Indicates whether Hello packets are being suppressed on this neighbor relationship.

interfaceName.description: Name of the local interface through which this neighbor is reachable.

ip_addr.description: IP address of the OSPF neighbor.

local_if_addr.description: Local interface IP address used to communicate with this neighbor.

neighbor_state.description: Current OSPF adjacency state with the neighbor.

oper_status.description: Operational status of the OSPF neighbor relationship.

priority.description: Router priority used in Designated Router election. Higher values indicate higher priority.

router_id.description: OSPF Router ID of the neighbor in dotted decimal format.

items.description: Appliance identifier in format 'X.NE' where X is a numeric ID.

autoReclassifyValues.description: Auto flow reclassify value applied to all appliances. Range: 0-65535.

ipsecPresharedKey.description: IPsec pre-shared key. Always null in GET responses for security.

overwriteExistingTunnels.description: When true, tunnel settings per WAN label are enabled.

tunnelMode.description: Global tunnel encapsulation mode for overlay tunnels.

enableIpslaRuleOrchestration.description: When true, IP SLA rules are automatically orchestrated.

enableInterRegionRouting.description: When true, inter-region routing is enabled for regional overlays.

OverlayManagerPropertiesPost.description: Request body for updating overlay manager properties.

autoReclassifyValues.description: Auto flow reclassify value applied to all appliances. Range: 0-65535.

enableAutoSaveOnVXOA.description: Auto-save configuration changes on appliances after each orchestration loop.

enableTemplateApply.description: Automatically apply templates to appliances during each orchestration loop.

enableIpslaRuleOrchestration.description: Enable IP SLA rule orchestration with overlay changes.

ipsecPresharedKey.description: IPsec pre-shared key for tunnel authentication. Omit to retain current value; empty string is invalid.

overwriteExistingTunnels.description: Enable tunnel settings per WAN label. When true, settings map is used for label-specific configuration.

tunnelMode.description: Global tunnel mode for overlay tunnels.

ipsecUdpPortIncrement.description: Port increment value for resolving IPsec UDP port conflicts between same-site appliances.

enableInterRegionRouting.description: Enable inter-region routing. When enabled, hub appliances are promoted in regional overlays.

WanLabelSettings.description: Tunnel configuration settings for a specific WAN label.

admin.description: Administrative state of the tunnel interface.

authenticationAlgorithm.description: IPsec authentication algorithm for data integrity verification.

autoMaxBandwidthEnabled.description: Automatically use maximum available bandwidth for the tunnel.

autoMtu.description: Automatically determine optimal MTU for the tunnel.

dhgroup.description: IKE Diffie-Hellman group number for key exchange.

dpdDelay.description: IKE Dead Peer Detection delay time in seconds. Range: 0-65535.

dpdRetry.description: IKE Dead Peer Detection retry count before declaring peer dead. Range: 0-65535.

dscp.description: Differentiated Services Code Point for QoS marking on tunnel packets.

encryptionAlgorithm.description: IPsec encryption algorithm. Empty string for auto-selection.

exchangeMode.description: IKE Phase 1 exchange mode. Auto-set to 'aggressive' when ikeVersion is 2.

fastfailWaitBase.description: Fastfail wait-time base offset in milliseconds. Range: 0-65535.

fastfailWaitRtt.description: Fastfail RTT multiplication factor for dynamic timeout. Range: 0-65535.

idStr.description: IKE identifier string for tunnel endpoint identification.

idType.description: IKE identifier type determining how endpoints are identified.

ikeAuthenticationAlgorithm.description: IKE authentication algorithm for Phase 1 negotiation.

ikeEncryptionAlgorithm.description: IKE encryption algorithm for Phase 1 negotiation.

ikeLifetime.description: IKE Phase 1 SA lifetime in minutes. Range: 0-65535.

ikeVersion.description: IKE protocol version. Version 2 auto-sets exchangeMode to aggressive.

ikeIdLocal.description: Local IKE identifier for tunnel authentication.

ikeIdRemote.description: Remote IKE identifier for tunnel authentication.

ipsecAntiReplayWindow.description: IPsec anti-replay window size for protection against replay attacks.

jitter.description: Jitter threshold in milliseconds for tunnel quality monitoring. Range: 0-65535.

latency.description: Latency threshold in milliseconds for tunnel quality monitoring. Range: 0-65535.

lifebytes.description: IPsec SA lifetime in megabytes. 0 means unlimited. Range: 0-4294967295.

lifetime.description: IPsec Phase 2 SA lifetime in minutes. Range: 30-65535.

lossVal.description: Packet loss threshold (0-1000 representing 0.0%-100.0%) for quality monitoring.

mode.description: Tunnel encapsulation mode for this WAN label.

mtu.description: Maximum Transmission Unit for tunnel packets in bytes. Range: 700-9000.

pfs.description: Enable Perfect Forward Secrecy for enhanced security.

pfsgroup.description: Perfect Forward Secrecy Diffie-Hellman group number.

reorderWait.description: Packet reorder wait time in milliseconds. Range: 0-500.

retryCount.description: Connection retry count in seconds before failover. Range: 3-60.

udpDestinationPort.description: UDP destination port for tunnel packets. Range: 1-65535.

udpFlows.description: Maximum number of UDP flows for the tunnel. Range: 1-1024.

endEntityCertificate.description: End entity certificate label for certificate-based auth. Required when peerAuthModes includes 1.

peerAuthModes.description: Peer authentication modes: 0=Pre-shared Key, 1=Certificate. Required for IPsec mode.

ppkMandatory.description: Post-quantum Pre-shared Key is mandatory for tunnel establishment.

ikePqcgroup.description: IKE Post-Quantum Cryptography key-exchange group. Must be 0 (disabled) or one of the allowed PQC groups from the active cipher profile. Only validated when mode is 'ipsec'.

ipsecPqcgroup.description: IPsec Post-Quantum Cryptography key-exchange group. Must be 0 (disabled) or one of the allowed PQC groups from the active cipher profile. Only validated when mode is 'ipsec'.

ipSecSuiteB.description: IPsec Suite B cryptographic algorithm selection.

latency.description: The latency (ms) to classify a tunnel in the brownout state.

loss.description: The percentage of loss to classify a tunnel in the 'brownout' state (when the other criteria is also met).

internetPolicy.description: Internet policy associated with this hub in the overlay

sum_rx_bytes.description: Total received bytes over the time period.

sum_tx_pkts.description: Total transmitted packets over the time period.

sum_rx_pkts.description: Total received packets over the time period.

max_tx_bytes_max.description: Maximum TX bytes with timestamp (format: value_timestamp).

max_rx_bytes_max.description: Maximum RX bytes with timestamp (format: value_timestamp).

max_tx_pkts_max.description: Maximum TX packets with timestamp (format: value_timestamp).

max_rx_pkts_max.description: Maximum RX packets with timestamp (format: value_timestamp).

max_ohead_rx_bytes_max.description: Maximum overhead RX bytes with timestamp.

max_ohead_tx_pkts_max.description: Maximum overhead TX packets with timestamp.

max_ohead_rx_pkts_max.description: Maximum overhead RX packets with timestamp.

crossConnect.description: An array of WAN interface label IDs to cross connect tunnels between
