destTunnelAlias.description: Tunnel alias on the destination appliance.

isPassThrough.description: True if this is a pass-through tunnel connecting to third-party services.

operStatus.description: Current operational status of the tunnel (e.g., 'Up', 'Down').

nePkToPhysicalTunnelsMap.description: Map of appliance nePk to their physical tunnels. Returned when querying all appliances.

nePksRequest.description: Request body containing appliance primary keys for the traceroute state query.

ApplianceUpgradeEntry.description: Configuration for initiating an appliance upgrade operation.

fromPortal.description: If true, the image is downloaded from Aruba Cloud Portal. Requires valid Portal registration.

imageName.description: Image filename for local/Portal images, or full URL when usingUrl is true. For local images, must exist in ftp/images directory.

installOption.description: Determines post-installation behavior. install_only: Install but don't activate. install_switch: Install and set as next boot. install_reboot: Install, switch, and reboot immediately.

usingUrl.description: If true, imageName contains an external URL to download the image from.

version.description: Target ECOS version including build number (format: x.x.x.x_build).

applianceImageId.description: Portal image ID for Portal-based upgrades. Used internally for download link generation.

randomString.description: Portal download token. Set automatically when fromPortal is true.

fromDiscovery.description: If true, targets discovered (not yet managed) appliances using discoveryIds instead of nePks.

discoveryIds.description: List of discovery IDs for upgrading discovered appliances. Required when fromDiscovery is true.

UpgradeAppliancesResponse.description: Response returned when an upgrade operation is successfully initiated.

clientKey.description: Unique key for tracking the background upgrade task. Use this key to poll for upgrade progress and status.

ValidateApplianceUpgradeEntry.description: Request parameters for validating ECOS firmware upgrade compatibility. Provide either versions array or imageUrl. All fields are optional with specific behaviors when omitted.

versions.description: ECOS versions to check compatibility against (without patch suffix, format: x.x.x.x). Required unless imageUrl is provided.

imageUrl.description: URL to an ECOS image ZIP file. Version is extracted from build_version.txt's BUILD_PROD_RELEASE field. Mutually exclusive with versions array.

appliances.description: Pre-populated appliance info array. If provided with data, skips database lookup and uses these appliances directly for validation.

ValidateApplianceUpgradeResponse.description: Validation response from Aruba Cloud Portal containing compatible ECOS upgrade paths for each appliance based on model, platform, and current version.

appliances.description: List of appliances with their model, platform, current version, and compatible upgrade versions determined by Portal.

orchSupports.description: Maximum ECOS version the current Orchestrator can manage. Appliances should not upgrade beyond this version.

orchestrator.description: Current Orchestrator software version (set automatically from GmsVersion).

versions.description: ECOS versions that were validated for upgrade compatibility.

versionUrl.description: Full version including patch number extracted from imageUrl's build_version.txt. Only present when imageUrl was provided in request. Format: x.x.x.x_build.

ChangePasswordBody.description: Request body for changing a user's password. Both current and new passwords are required.

oldPassword.description: The user's current password. Must match the existing password stored in the system.

newPassword.description: The new password. Must be 8-64 characters with uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character. Cannot be the same as the old password. Cannot contain username or match common words/password history.

DynamicPreferencesSaveForUser.description: Legacy schema for saving user preferences. Use DynamicTopologyConfigRequest instead.

ForgotPasswordBody.description: Request body for initiating a password reset. Provide either username or email address.

userName.description: User identifier for password reset. Can be the username or email address. If email is provided and no user matches by username, lookup by email is attempted.

NewTfaKeyResponse.description: Response containing a QR code barcode for TOTP two-factor authentication setup. The QR code contains an otpauth:// URL that can be scanned by authenticator apps.

barcodeBase64Jpeg.description: Base64-encoded JPEG image of a QR code containing the TOTP secret key. Scan with Google Authenticator, Authy, or similar TOTP apps. The QR code encodes an otpauth:// URL with the secret, issuer (HPE Aruba Networking EdgeConnect Enterprise Orchestrator), and username.

ResetPasswordBody.description: Request body for resetting a user's password. Requires either 'id' (from email reset link) or 'username' to identify the user.

id.description: Reset password token from the email link. Either 'id' or 'username' must be provided. Token expires after 4 days.

username.description: Username to reset password for. Used when 'id' is not provided. Either 'id' or 'username' must be provided.

password.description: New password. Must be 8-64 characters with uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character. Cannot contain username.

confirmPassword.description: Must match the password field exactly for confirmation.

tfaEmail.description: Enable email-based two-factor authentication. Sends a code to user's email on login.

tfaApp.description: Enable app-based (TOTP) two-factor authentication. Uses authenticator apps like Google Authenticator.

newTfaCode.description: Generate a new TOTP secret key. Returns a QR code in the response when true and tfaApp is enabled.

SaveUpdateUserBody.description: Request body for creating or updating a user account.

username.description: Login username. Must be alphanumeric with underscores, dots, dashes, or a valid email format. Cannot be changed after creation.

firstName.description: User's first name for display purposes.

lastName.description: User's last name for display purposes.

email.description: User's email address. Required if password is not provided (for new user invitation). Used for password reset and email-based TFA.

phone.description: User's phone number for contact purposes.

password.description: User's password. Must be 8-64 characters with uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character. Cannot contain username. Leave empty to send password reset email (requires email).

repeatPassword.description: Must match the password field exactly for confirmation.

role.description: User role determining permissions. Admin Manager has full read/write access. Network Monitor has read-only access.

status.description: Account status. Active users can log in. Inactive users are disabled but retained in the system.

isTwoFactorEmail.description: Enable email-based two-factor authentication. On cloud orchestrator, at least one TFA method must be enabled.

isTwoFactorTime.description: Enable app-based (TOTP) two-factor authentication. On cloud orchestrator, at least one TFA method must be enabled.

userPk.description: Primary key of the user. Leave empty for new user creation. Required for updates to identify the user record.

createDisplayTime.description: Display-formatted creation time. Optional field for UI purposes.

isPasswordInit.description: Indicates if user has set initial password. Used during updates to determine if email is required.

UserInfoResponse.description: User account information returned by the GET /users endpoint.

userPk.description: Unique primary key identifier for the user.

username.description: Login username. Can be alphanumeric with underscores, dots, dashes, or a valid email format.

email.description: User's email address for notifications and password reset.

password.description: Always returned as empty string for security.

salt.description: Always returned as empty string for security.

createTime.description: Account creation timestamp in milliseconds since epoch.

status.description: Account status. Active users can log in; Inactive users are disabled.

role.description: User role. Admin Manager has full access; Network Monitor has read-only access.

isCurrentlyLoggedIn.description: Indicates if the user currently has an active session.

isPasswordInit.description: Indicates if the user has set an initial password.

lastLoginS.description: Last successful login timestamp in seconds since epoch.

expireTime.description: Password expiration timestamp in milliseconds. 0 means no expiration.

UsersGetItem.description: Legacy schema for user information (deprecated, use UserInfoResponse).

UsersGetNotifyPasswordExpiry.description: Password expiry notification status for the authenticated user.

isLocalUser.description: Indicates if the user exists in the local database. False for SSO/LDAP users not stored locally.

notifyPasswordExpiry.description: True if password is expiring within the configured 'notifyPasswordExpiryDays' threshold (5-30 days). Always false if password expiration is disabled.

daysUntilExpiration.description: Days remaining until password expires. Returns 0 if password expiration is disabled or user is non-local.

PasswordSettings.description: Password policy configuration for an appliance. Controls password complexity, expiration, history, and user inactivity settings.

passwordMinLen.description: Minimum required password length. Must be between 8 and 64 characters.

passwordExpireDays.description: Number of days before password expires and user must create a new password. Must be between 30 and 360.

passwordHistoryCount.description: Number of previous passwords remembered to prevent reuse. Must be between 4 and 8.

notifyPasswordExpiryDays.description: Days before expiration to start notifying user about upcoming password expiry. Must be between 5 and 30.

userInactiveDays.description: Days of user inactivity before account is disabled. Set to 0 to disable this feature, or between 30 and 360 to enable.

Session.description: Details of an active user session on the appliance.

username.description: Username of the logged-in user.

gid.description: Group ID of the user (0 for admin, 1001 for monitor).

port.description: Connection type/interface. Typically 'web' for browser sessions or 'ssh' for CLI sessions.

remote_host.description: IP address of the remote client that initiated the session.

login_time.description: Timestamp when the session was initiated.

idle_time.description: Duration the session has been idle (format: HH:MM:SS).

SessionMap.description: A dynamic map where each key is a session number (starting from 1) and value is the Session object.

User.description: User account details for an appliance user.

self.description: The username of this account.

gid.description: Group ID representing the user's role. Value 0 indicates admin role, 1001 indicates monitor (read-only) role.

enable.description: Whether the user account is enabled (active) or disabled.

password.description: The user's password (typically masked in responses).

UserAccount.description: Container for user accounts and active sessions on an appliance.

users.description: Map of user accounts keyed by username.

sessions.description: Map of active sessions keyed by session number.

UserMap.description: A dynamic map where each key is a username and value is the User object.

Enable.description: Represents the global Routing Segmentation (VRF) enable/disable state in Orchestrator.

enable.description: Controls whether Routing Segmentation (VRF) is enabled globally. When true, network traffic can be segmented into multiple VRFs. When false (default), all traffic uses the default segment.

OrchestrationSecurityMapOptions.description: Options controlling security policy orchestration behavior.

merge.description: When false, replaces existing security policies in orchestration range. When true, merges with existing policies.

templateApply.description: Set to true for standard security policies orchestration. Set to false for template-based application.

OrchestrationSecurityMapSettings.description: Logging configuration settings for security policy events.

PolicyRuleMatch.description: Match criteria for identifying traffic to apply DNAT translation. At least one match condition should be specified.

acl.description: Name of an access control list (ACL) to match against traffic.

PolicyRuleMatchStr.description: String-based match criteria for traffic selection.

dst_ip.description: Destination IP address or subnet to match. Can be single IP or CIDR notation.

PolicyRuleSet.description: Actions to perform on matched traffic, including destination VRF and IP translation.

dst_vrf.description: Target VRF segment ID for the translated traffic. Traffic will be routed to this segment.

trans_dst_ip.description: Translated destination IP address. The original destination IP will be replaced with this value.

PostSegment.description: Request body for creating a new routing segment (VRF). Only the name field is required; the segment ID is auto-generated by the system.

name.description: Unique name for the segment. Must contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores. Cannot be 'Default' (reserved for segment ID 0).

SecurityMaps.description: Container for security policies. Contains 'map1' key with zone-to-zone policy mappings.

UpdateSegment.description: Request body for updating an existing routing segment (VRF). Only name and comment can be modified.

name.description: New name for the segment. Must be unique across all segments, contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores, and cannot be 'Default'.

comment.description: Optional description or notes for the segment.

VRFPolicyLoggingLevel.description: Logging level configuration for implicit firewall drops.

imp_fw_drop.description: Logging level for implicit firewall drops. Empty string disables logging.

VRFPolicyMap.description: Map of segment IDs to their DNAT policy rules. Keys are segment identifiers (integers as strings).

VRFPolicyRule.description: A single DNAT policy rule defining match criteria and translation actions.

enable.description: Whether this rule is active. Disabled rules are not applied to traffic.

comment.description: Optional user-defined description of the rule's purpose.
comment.example: DNAT rule for web traffic to internal server

gms_marked.description: Internal flag indicating if this rule was created by Orchestrator (GMS). Used for tracking Orchestrator-managed configurations.

misc.description: Miscellaneous rule metadata or configuration options.

VRFPolicyRuleMap.description: Map of DNAT policy rules for a single source segment. Each key is a priority number string, and the value is a VRFPolicyRule defining the DNAT translation.

VRFPolicyRules.description: Map of priority numbers to policy rules. Keys are rule priorities (integers as strings), lower values indicate higher priority.

VRFSecurityPolicies.description: Security policies configuration for zone-based firewall rules between routing segments.

data.description: Required. Contains zone-to-zone security policies keyed by 'map1'.

options.description: Options controlling how policies are applied during orchestration.

settings.description: Logging settings for security policy events.

VRFSegment.description: Represents a routing segment (VRF) configuration in Orchestrator. Each segment isolates network traffic and can have its own routing, firewall, and NAT policies.

id.description: Unique identifier for the segment. 0 is reserved for the default segment. Custom segments use IDs 1-65400.

name.description: Human-readable name for the segment. Must be unique and contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores. 'Default' is reserved for segment ID 0.

status.description: Segment status flag. 0 indicates normal/active status.

comment.description: Optional user-provided description for the segment.

VRFSegmentsMap.description: Map of all routing segments keyed by segment ID string. Always includes the default segment (id=0). Used when retrieving all segments without specifying an id parameter.

VRFSnatEnable.description: Configuration for an Inter-Segment SNAT rule between two network segments.

enable.description: Enables or disables the SNAT rule for traffic between the source and destination segments.

gms_marked.description: Indicates whether this rule was configured via Orchestrator (true) or directly on the appliance (false). Rules marked by Orchestrator take precedence.

comment.description: Optional user-defined comment or description for this SNAT rule.

VRFSnatMaps.description: Map of Inter-Segment SNAT enable/disable configurations keyed by segment pair identifier. Each key is in format 'sourceSegmentId_destinationSegmentId'. Controls whether Source NAT is applied for traffic flowing between specific segment pairs.

0_1.comment: Disable SNAT from Default to Production

1_2.comment: Enable SNAT from Production to Development

SnatMapsConfig.description: A map of Inter-Segment SNAT configurations. Keys are segment pair identifiers in format 'SourceSegmentId_DestinationSegmentId'.

1_2.comment: Enable SNAT from segment 1 to segment 2

VRRP_GET.description: VRRP instance configuration and state information

groupId.description: VRRP group identifier shared by peers in a redundancy group. Must be unique per interface.

interface.description: Network interface name for VRRP peering. Supports wan, lan, and subinterfaces.

enable.description: Administrative state of the VRRP instance.

vipaddr.description: Virtual IP address shared by the VRRP group. Must not match any existing interface IP on the appliance. Version 2 supports IPv4 only; version 3 supports IPv4 and IPv6.

adv_timer.description: Advertisement interval in seconds between VRRP hello messages.

priority.description: Priority value for master election. Higher value wins. The appliance with highest priority becomes VRRP Master.

preempt.description: When true, a higher-priority appliance will reclaim master role upon recovery. When false, current master retains role.

auth.description: Simple text authentication string for VRRP v2. Not supported in VRRP v3.

desc.description: User-defined description for the VRRP instance.

pkt_trace.description: Enable packet tracing for VRRP debugging purposes.

holddown.description: Holddown timer in seconds before transitioning to master state after detecting master failure.

mode.description: Current operational state of the VRRP instance.

masterip.description: IP address of the current VRRP master router.

uptime.description: Duration since the VRRP instance entered its current state.

master_transitions.description: Count of state transitions between Master and Backup. High values may indicate configuration or network issues.

vipowner.description: Indicates if the appliance owns the virtual IP. Always false for Silver Peak appliances as they cannot use their own IPs as VRRP VIPs.

vmac.description: Virtual MAC address used by the VRRP instance. Physical appliances use format 00-00-5E-00-01-{VRID}. Virtual appliances use the interface's assigned MAC.

vtiConfig.description: Map of VTI interface names (e.g., 'vti0', 'vti1') to their configuration details.

vtiConfigDetail.description: Configuration details for a single VTI interface.

admin.description: Administrative state of the interface. True enables the interface, false disables it.

ipaddr.description: IPv4 address assigned to the VTI interface. Used as the local endpoint for the tunnel.

label.description: User-defined label for identifying the VTI interface. Used for route-label based steering.

nmask.description: Network mask in CIDR notation (prefix length). Valid range: 0-32.

side.description: Network side assignment. Determines traffic flow direction for security policies.

tunnel.description: Associated third-party passthrough tunnel alias (e.g., IPsec tunnel name). Links VTI to specific tunnel configuration.

vrf_id.description: VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) segment ID. 0 represents the default segment.

zone.description: Security zone ID for firewall policy application. Zones group interfaces for policy enforcement.

errorNotAvailable.description: Error response when VXLAN configuration is not available on the appliance or cached data is empty.

ERROR.description: Error code indicating configuration is not available.

segVniMap.description: Map of VRF segment IDs to their VXLAN VNI configurations. Keys are VRF IDs as strings (e.g., '0', '1', '2').

tunnelStateEntry.description: Connection state information for a specific VXLAN tunnel.

remoteIp.description: Remote VTEP IP address for this tunnel.

localIp.description: Local VTEP IP address for this tunnel.

state.description: Connection state of the tunnel (e.g., 'established', 'connecting', 'disconnected').

tunnelStatsEntry.description: Traffic statistics for a specific VXLAN tunnel.

state.description: Current operational state of the tunnel (e.g., 'up', 'down').

rxPkts.description: Number of packets received on this tunnel.

txPkts.description: Number of packets transmitted on this tunnel.

vniConfigMap.description: VNI configuration for a specific VRF segment including network identifier, zone assignment, and fallback role.

vni.description: VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI) assigned to this VRF segment. Range: 1-16777215.

zoneId.description: Security zone identifier associated with this VRF segment. Used for firewall policy enforcement.

role.description: Fallback role identifier for traffic handling. Determines behavior when primary path is unavailable.

vniStatsEntry.description: Traffic statistics for a specific VNI (VXLAN Network Identifier).

rxPkts.description: Number of packets received on this VNI.

txPkts.description: Number of packets transmitted on this VNI.

rxBytes.description: Number of bytes received on this VNI.

txBytes.description: Number of bytes transmitted on this VNI.

vxlanConfig.description: VXLAN tunnel endpoint configuration containing interface and port settings.

port.description: Destination UDP port for VXLAN encapsulation. Standard IANA-assigned port is 4789.

vtepIf.description: VTEP (VXLAN Tunnel Endpoint) source interface name used for tunnel origination (e.g., 'lo0'). Only loopback interfaces from the default segment are supported. Valid format: 'lo' followed by a number from 0-99999.

vxlanStateObj.description: VXLAN operational state containing VNI statistics, tunnel statistics, and tunnel state information for monitoring overlay network health.

vniStats.description: Map of VNI IDs to their traffic statistics. Keys are VNI identifiers as strings.

tunnelStats.description: Map of tunnel identifiers to their traffic statistics. Keys are tunnel names or IDs.

tunnelState.description: Map of tunnel identifiers to their connection state information. Keys are tunnel names or IDs.

VxoaHostname.description: Request object for changing an appliance hostname.

hostname.description: The new hostname to assign to the appliance. Should follow valid hostname conventions (alphanumeric characters and hyphens).

WCCPGroupLevelState.description: Container for all WCCP service group states. Keys are service group IDs.

WCCPSystemLevelState.description: System-level operational state for WCCP on the appliance.

debug_all.description: Combined debug output from all WCCP components. Empty when debugging is disabled.

debug_global.description: Global WCCP debug information. Empty when no global debug data available.

is_alive.description: Indicates whether WCCP service is running. Values: 'yes' (running), 'no' (stopped).

proto_ver.description: WCCP protocol version in use. Common values: '1.0', '2.0'.

WccpConfigSystem.description: WCCP system-level configuration settings for the appliance.

enable.description: Indicates whether WCCP is enabled on the appliance. When true, WCCP service is active.

mcast_ttl.description: Multicast Time-To-Live (TTL) value for WCCP packets. Controls how many network hops the packets can traverse. Valid range: 1-255.

compatibility.description: WCCP service group compatibility mode. Valid values: ios, nexus

force_l2_return.description: WCCP service group force l2 return

hash_dst_ip.description: WCCP service group hash destination ip

hash_dst_port.description: WCCP service group hash destination port

hash_src_ip.description: WCCP service group hash source ip

hash_src_port.description: WCCP service group hash source port

mask_dst_ip.description: WCCP service group mask destination ip

mask_dst_port.description: WCCP service group mask destination port

mask_src_ip.description: WCCP service group mask source ip

mask_src_port.description: WCCP service group mask source port

password.description: WCCP service group password

priority.description: WCCP service group priority. Valid range: [0, 255].

ipaddr.description: WCCP service group router IP address.

self.description: Integer value of service group Id

WccpGroupState.description: Operational state information for a single WCCP service group.

app_id.description: Application identifier for the WCCP service group.

assignment.description: Load balancing assignment method. Values: 'hash' or 'mask'.

debug.description: Debug output for troubleshooting. Empty when no debug info available.

num_appliances.description: Number of web cache appliances participating in this service group.

num_routers.description: Number of routers participating in this service group.

oper.description: Operational status of the service group. Values: 'up' (operational), 'down' (not operational).

self.description: Service group identifier (0-255). Well-known IDs: 0=HTTP, 51-99=user-defined.

uptime.description: Time in seconds since the service group became operational.

WccpState.description: Complete WCCP operational state including system-level and per-group information.

group.description: Per-group operational state. Contains one entry per configured service group.

system.description: System-level WCCP state including alive status and protocol version.

VrfSegmentZoneDetail.description: Complete zone-to-VRF segment mapping with full details. Represents a single zone within a specific VRF segment.

zoneId.description: Unique zone ID across all VRF segments. Zone ID 0 is the system Default zone. Range is 1-135 without VRF or 1-65400 with VRF enabled.

zoneName.description: Zone name. Default value is empty string if not set. 'Default' is the reserved system zone name.

vrfId.description: VRF segment ID. 0 represents the Default VRF segment which always exists.

vrfName.description: VRF segment name. Default value is empty string if not set. 'Default' is the name of segment ID 0.

VrfSegmentZonesMapResponse.description: Flat list of all zone-to-VRF segment mappings. Each entry contains complete details about a zone and its associated VRF segment. Unknown zone indices are automatically filtered out.

VrfZonesMap.description: Hierarchical map of VRF segment IDs (as string keys) to their zone index maps. The outer keys are VRF segment IDs (0 is the Default segment). The inner keys are zone indices within each segment. Implemented as HashMap<Integer, ZonesIndexMap> in the backend.

x-constraints.outerKey: VRF segment ID (integer as string). 0 = Default segment
x-constraints.filteredIndices: Zone index 255 (unknown) is automatically filtered out
x-constraints.defaultSegment: Segment ID 0 (Default) always exists when VRF zones are configured

name.description: Zone name. Must contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores. Cannot be 'Default'.

enable.description: Whether End-to-End Zone-Based Firewall is enabled. Cannot be disabled when Routing Segmentation is active.

ZoneIndexMap.description: Map of zone indices (0-254) to VRF zone objects within a VRF segment. Index 255 is reserved for unknown zones and is filtered out. Implemented as a TreeMap for consistent ordering.

Zones.description: Map of zone IDs (as strings) to zone objects

ZonesPostRequest.description: Request body for creating/updating zones. Map of zone IDs (as string keys) to zone objects. Replaces all existing zones - omit a zone to delete it.

nePkRequired.name: nePk
nePkRequired.description: Network Element Primary Key - unique appliance identifier assigned by Orchestrator. Format: '<id>.NE' (e.g., '0.NE', '10.NE').

nePkOptional.name: nePk
nePkOptional.description: Network Element Primary Key - unique appliance identifier assigned by Orchestrator. Format: '<id>.NE' (e.g., '0.NE', '10.NE'). When omitted, results are returned for all appliances.
